jobs.description:
Job Description

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

The Care Manager I (Masters Social Work) coordinate patients’ needs through the continuum of care which can include from pre-admission through post discharge plans. This role works in collaboration with the physicians, nurses, clinical staff, and community agencies to identify and arrange for appropriate care.

Reviews clinician assessments and patients’ financial, family and psychosocial support to develop comprehensive care and/or discharge plans. May focus more heavily on a specific aspect of Care Management like discharge planning, utilization review, and/or providing psychosocial support.

May review records to assess for appropriate admission status, level of care, payer source, and UR contracts to validate billing. May provide psychodynamic intervention and crisis counseling to support patients and families. Educates patients and families on their healthcare options and connects them with resources.

Documents pertinent patient issues, contacts and plans on the medical records. Is a mandated reporter for elder, child, and spousal abuse. The Community Care role specifically provides Care Management support to high-risk, homeless and mental health population. Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Fulfills mandatory stroke education requirements per certification agency

Positions Requirements Depend On Licensure And Are As Follows

Care Manager (MSW) – Master’s degree in Social Work (MSW) required. One year of MSW experience in an acute healthcare setting preferred.

About Us

Hoag Memorial Hospital Presbyterian is a nonprofit regional health care delivery network in Orange County, California, consisting of three acute-care hospitals with sixteen urgent care centers, eleven health centers and a network of more than1,800 physicians, 100 allied health members, 8,000 employees, and 2,000 volunteers. More than 30,000 inpatients and 550,000 outpatients choose Hoag each year.

For over 70 years, Hoag has delivered a level of personalized care that is unsurpassed among Orange County’s health care providers. Since 1952, Hoag has served the local communities and continues its mission to provide the highest quality health care services through the core strategies of quality and service, people, physician partnerships, strategic growth, financial stewardship, community benefit and philanthropy.

Hoag offers a comprehensive blend of health care services including six institutes providing specialized care in the areas of cancer, heart and vascular, neurosciences, women's health, orthopedics, and digestive health through our institutes.

Hoag was the highest ranked hospital in Orange County in the 2024-2025 U.S. News &World Report, the only Orange County hospital ranked in the top 10 for California. The organization was ranked the #5 hospital in the Los Angeles Metro Area and the #10 hospital in California.

To learn more about Hoag’s awards and accreditations, visit: https://www.hoag.org/about-hoag/awards-accreditations/ .

Hoag is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. Hoag is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all employees and providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Hoag hires a diverse group of people in a manner that allows them to reach their full potential in the pursuit of organizational objectives.

jobs.description:
About Perfected

With empathy at its core, Perfected serves as a bridge between individuals impacted by injury or catastrophe and the law firms that advocate for their voices. We are currently seeking two bilingual (English and Spanish) Case Managers to join our Pasadena, CA office in support of the LA Fire Justice campaign. If that sounds like you, and your qualifications are a good match, we look forward to hearing from you!

About the Role

The Case Manager
is responsible for a docket of cases that need to be moved through different milestones of the client’s case development journey. The Case Manager will be cross-trained in all areas of case management: Intake Qualification, Medical Record Retrieval Coordination, Medical Record Review, Plaintiff Form Fulfillment, Client Engagement, Quality Assurance, and Post Settlement Coordination. In addition to communication, via calls, emails, and texts, the Case Manager will assist clients in person when they visit the office.

What You’ll Do

Gathers and interprets data to develop actionable next steps to optimize best-case results.
Undertakes a diverse range of quality assurance tasks, each assigned based on the case's status (Intake, Onboarding, Medical Record Retrieval, Medical Record Review, and Plaintiff Form Fulfillment).
Responsible for inbound and outbound communication (calls/emails/texts) with clients to obtain case-related details, confirm information, complete documentation/questionnaires, and provide case and settlement status updates. 
Works with external partners such as experts, appraisers, and contractors to validate and maximize client’s claims.
Submits client’s case filing, and questionnaires prior to court set deadlines.
Supports Community Outreach needs such as fielding phone calls, taking 1:1 appointments, and supporting weekly events as needed.
In person communication with clients.
Empathetic and concise when communicating with clients. Having patience and leading with empathy is a requirement.
Responsible for managing assigned cases.
Responsible for managing priorities to help meet and maintain production goals and Service Level Agreements (SLAs). 
Responsible for maintaining quality guidelines. 
Ensures all assigned cases maintain accurate and up-to-date information and details.
Conducts audits and reviews of client files to ensure accuracy, completeness, and adherence to standards.
Maintains knowledge on the torts in which we are supporting.
Ability and willingness to work overtime as needed. Must be available to work extended hours, including evenings and/or weekends, to meet critical deadlines when required by operational demands.
Perform other duties as assigned.

What You Bring

Bachelor's Degree or similar experience.
1+ years of experience in the mass tort industry and/or a similar role.
1+ years of legal knowledge/ case management.
1+ years in customer service.
1+ years of previous experience handling high call volumes with tact and empathy.
Bilingual in Spanish is considered a required qualification for this role.
Strong computer skills, including Salesforce, Google Sheets, Microsoft Office.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

Skills and Abilities

Strong interpersonal skills capable of maintaining strong relationships.
Detail-oriented and excellent multitasking skills.
Strong organizational abilities.
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.
Strong analytical skills.
Problem-solving skills.
Comfortable operating in a process-driven environment. 
Able to remain calm under pressure.
Ability to learn and adapt to change quickly.
Ability to work independently and as a team player.

Physical Requirements

Frequent need for oral, written, and auditory communication.
Prolonged periods working on a computer.
Ability to sit for long periods of time.
Prolonged periods working on a computer.
Frequent repetitive hand and wrist motions.
Ability to work in a fast paced and sometimes stressful services environment.

PTO (15 days, earned on an accrual basis; increases at 3rd and 5th anniversary), sick leave (10 days, earned on an accrual basis), paid holidays (14) and floating holidays (2 days).

jobs.title: RN Case Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We are VITAS Healthcare, the nation’s leading end-of-life care provider since 1978.

Our hospice organization kickstarts careers in caring, promotes from within, and provides a nationally recognized best-in-class employee experience. Supported by industry-leading experts and a growing network of programs in 15+ states, VITAS empowers team members to grow toward their goals while transforming patients’ lives.

Our priority is to care: For our patients, for each other, and for the future.

Salary: $55-$59/hr

What You’ll Do

As a home care registered nurse (RN), you will ensure hospice patients are comfortable and forge compassionate, meaningful connections with the people in their lives.

This is important work that comes with equal responsibility. Patients and families trust VITAS nurses to guide them through the end-of-life journey, and maintaining that trust is our highest priority.

You will be a respected member of our team, both as a caregiver and as a hospice educator. You will be entrusted with the autonomy to make care decisions at the bedside, ensuring not a moment is wasted in bringing comfort to your patients.

You will help patients and their loved ones understand and embrace the palliative—rather than curative—nature of hospice and the benefits of comfort-focused end-of-life care.

WHERE YOU’LL WORK

Each day is different. You will spend most of your time caring for hospice patients wherever they call home, whether that means a private residence or an assisted living/skilled nursing facility. Most VITAS nurses make 4-6 visits each day.

Once a week, you’ll visit the local program office to meet with an interdisciplinary team, including social workers, physicians, chaplains, and nurses, who collaborate to provide holistic support for the patients and families we serve.

What’s Expected From You

A VITAS nurse is the end-of-life caregiver everyone deserves. In addition to having your RN license, at least two years of nursing experience, and reliable transportation, you'll approach your work with the traits that make the VITAS Difference: Commitment, Compassion, and a Can-do Attitude.

You will keep patient welfare at the center of everything you do, giving your best each day in service of our core commitment: Extending comfort and dignity to all people at the end of their life’s journey.

Qualifications

Currently licensed to practice nursing in the state where the VITAS program is located.
A minimum of two years of nursing experience in hospice, home health, or community health in the last five years.
Equivalent experience or licensure may be considered

jobs.title: Privacy Program Specialist, Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

Your Role

The Privacy Office is responsible for development, implementation, and oversight of Blue Shield’s Privacy Program. The Privacy Program ensures that Blue Shield and its affiliated covered entities, including Blue Shield of California Promise Health Plan, are in compliance with state and federal privacy laws and regulations, including the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act of 2009 (HITECH), and California’s Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA). The Privacy Program Specialist, Consultant reports to the Privacy Office Sr. Manager and plays an essential role in advancing and enforcing Blue Shield’s Privacy Program.

Responsibilities

Your Work

In this role, you will:

Be responsible for the oversight of Blue Shield's compliance with state and federal privacy laws, including the privacy component of HIPAA and HITECH
The majority of this role involves leading assigned privacy investigations, timely and accurately document case files, direct investigations into root cause analysis, address mitigation, and work with impacted business units to develop and complete corrective action for remediation and to minimize risk of recurrence
Consult with internal clients to review and provide privacy guidance about proposed projects and initiatives and serve as a privacy subject matter expert
Respond to privacy-related requests and inquiries
Develop and assist with the implementation of workforce privacy training programs, privacy policies, desk-level procedures, resource guides, job aids, and other educational tools
Act as a liaison with regulatory enforcement agencies to address technical assistance letters, investigation compliance reviews, audits, and other related reviews
Assist, evaluate, and determine appropriateness of ad hoc requests from internal clients to disclose protected health information (PHI) to third parties and/or to allow third parties access to, or use of, Blue Shield PHI
Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Your Knowledge and Experience

Required

Requires a bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree
Requires 7 years of prior relevant experience
Requires prior experience in healthcare privacy, cybersecurity incident management, investigative services, or another related field
Requires a solid understanding of state and federal privacy laws, including HIPAA/HITECH, CMIA, and privacy-related consumer protections laws, such as the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), as well as knowledge of Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) privacy requirements for Medi-Cal Managed Care Health Plans and Centers for Medicare or Medi-Cal and Medicaid (CMS) Medicare or Medi-Cal Managed Care Plans
Requires excellent organizational skills and strong independent judgment, problem-solving, critical and analytical thinking skills, including an exceptional “moral compass” and work ethic
Requires ability to work collaboratively in a team, perform duties with minimal supervision, multi-task, and to deliver a quality work product in a highly regulated, demanding, and constantly changing corporate environment
Requires proficiency in Microsoft Word, Access, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

Preferred

Possesses extensive experience in directly handling investigations
Privacy healthcare-related experience that includes a familiarity with Privacy Impact Assessments and Data Protection Impact Assessments; auditing and monitoring; investigating, managing, and reporting privacy incidents; health information management
CIPP/US Certification or HCCA CHPC Certification
Experience and knowledge of compliance or privacy incident management software

Hybrid

This role requires employees to be in-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week.

Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.

About Us

About Blue Shield of California

As of January 2025, Blue Shield of California became a subsidiary of Ascendiun. Ascendiun is a nonprofit corporate entity that is the parent to a family of organizations including Blue Shield of California and its subsidiary, Blue Shield of California Promise Health Plan; Altais, a clinical services company; and Stellarus, a company designed to scale healthcare solutions. Together, these organizations are referred to as the Ascendiun Family of Companies.

At Blue Shield of California, our mission is to create a healthcare system worthy of our family and friends and sustainably affordable. We are transforming health care in a way that genuinely serves our nonprofit mission by lowering costs, improving quality, and enhancing the member and physician experience.

To achieve our mission, we foster an environment where all employees can thrive and contribute fully to address the needs of the various communities we serve. We are committed to creating and maintaining a supportive workplace that upholds our values and advances our goals.

Blue Shield is a U.S. News Best Company to work for, a Deloitte U.S. Best Managed Company and a Top 100 Inspiring Workplace. We were recognized by Fair360 as a Top Regional Company, and one of the 50 most community-minded companies in the United States by Points of Light. Here at Blue Shield, we strive to make a positive change across our industry and communities – join us!

Our Values:

Honest. We hold ourselves to the highest ethical and integrity standards. We build trust by doing what we say we're going to do and by acknowledging and correcting where we fall short.
Human. We strive to listen and communicate effectively, showing empathy by understanding others' perspectives.
Courageous. We stand up for what we believe in and are committed to the hard work necessary to achieve our ambitious goals.

Our Workplace Model

We believe in fostering a workplace environment that balances purposeful in-person collaboration with flexibility - providing clear expectations while respecting the diverse needs of our workforce. Our workplace model is designed around intentional in-person interaction, collaboration, connection, creativity and flexibility:

For most teams, this means coming into the office two days per week.
Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location, out of state employees, and employees in certain member-facing roles should work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.
For employees with medical conditions that may impact their ability to work in-office, we are committed to engaging in an interactive process and providing reasonable accommodations to ensure their work environment is conducive to their success and well-being.

The Company reserves the right to require more presence in the office based on business needs, and requirements are subject to change with periodic reviews.

jobs.description:
Pinterest is looking for a Merch Program Manager (contractor) to run the day-to-day operations of our centralized merch program and Pinterest Merch Storefront. This role will sit on the Workplace Experience team and partner closely with Events, People, Brand, Comms, Finance, and Procurement to bring our merch strategy to life through excellent execution.
You will manage the end-to-end operational workflow for Pinterest-branded merchandise, while bringing forward thoughtful strategy recommendations and driving their implementation across the program if approved. Strategy, roadmap, and final policy decisions will remain with the internal merch program lead that you will report to.
What you’ll do

Facilitate day-to-day operations of the Pinterest Merch Storefront; ensuring a smooth, scalable experience for internal and external purchasers.
Coordinate with our merch vendor (single vendor) on quotes, timelines, samples, production status, tracking, and issue resolution for orders, gift campaigns, and special projects.
Approve restocks and make recommendations to replace or discontinue
Ensure our vendor is set up for success with clear briefs, timelines, and context for key launches and programs.
Act as the first point of contact for merch program, questions and requests (e.g., via shared aliases and forms), triaging inquiries and guiding partners to the right paths
Partner closely with Events and Workplace teammates to align merch solutions with internal events, on-sites, and other experience programs.
Assist two other internal teams to work with the vendor and align their business gifting needs and program goals. Assisting with troubleshooting as it arises.
Deliver change management and education across key stakeholder groups (e.g., ABPs, managers, Sales, Recruiting, I&B, L&D), including trainings, office hours, and ongoing communications.
Draft guidelines into clear playbooks, FAQs, templates, and Internal Internet content; keep all documentation up to date as the program evolves
Help plan and execute seasonal program launches, opt out/donation/credit workflows, and catalog updates; coordinating timelines, testing flows, and capturing feedback.
Be knowledgeable and champion our guiding principles for merch (brand expression, sustainability, social impact, and responsible spend) in day-to-day decisions, recommending options that balance impact, experience, and budget.
Support governance and compliance by ensuring all orders follow purchasing guidelines, approved vendor pathways, and the correct coding, in partnership with Finance and Procurement.
Flag edge cases and exceptions to the internal merch program lead for decisions, and help operationalize approved changes in playbooks and processes.
Weekly: Provide updates in 1:1s with the merch program lead regarding operational gaps, pain points, or program successes.
Monthly: Pull and interpret storefront dashboards for inventory decision making; propose process improvements and escalate strategic or policy decisions to the internal merch program lead.
Quarterly: Interpret quarterly finance reports; surface insights and recommendations to the merch program lead.
Manage all onsite merch-related tasks and logistics including:
Keeping the team storage closet organized and ensure inventory, supplies, and samples are stored in an organized and accessible way.
Receive product samples and organize for easy review and decision-making.
Sort, pack, and ship event merch as needed to support internal activations and programs.
Set up merch pop-ups, displays and help internal buyers as-needed to review samples in person.
Provide additional support as needed for the team, including onsite event production support.

You’ll Be Successful in This Role if You Have:

2-4 years in program or operations management in a related area (workplace, events, marketing operations, merchandising, or similar).
Experience administering a merch, swag, gifting, or e-commerce program (or a strong adjacent operations background with an interest in merch).
Demonstrated success managing complex operational workflows end-to-end, including intake, prioritization, execution, and follow-through.
Strong vendor management skills: you’re comfortable coordinating with external partners on timelines, scope, budgets, and quality, and escalating when needed.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; you can translate policy into clear, friendly guidelines, templates, and trainings for a range of stakeholders.
High level of comfort with spreadsheets and reporting tools (e.g., Google Sheets) to track budgets, credits, orders, and program performance.
Detail-oriented and highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent deadlines and stakeholders.
A service-minded, collaborative working style — you enjoy helping internal partners navigate new processes and find the right merch solutions.
AI Forward: Comfort using AI tools and proactively identifies ways to streamline workflows using AI, while exercising strong judgment by editing for quality and ensuring accuracy and compliance
Comfortable operating as a contractor: you bring forward thoughtful recommendations and handle execution, while deferring final strategy, policy, and exception decisions to the internal merch program lead.

We encourage qualified candidates who are passionate about supporting survivors of human trafficking to apply. Candidates who previously applied do not need to reapply, as prior applications remain on file and may continue to be considered.

The Human Trafficking Case Manager is responsible for providing client-centered crisis intervention, client advocacy, safety planning, supportive counseling, case management, and referrals for adult survivors of trafficking. The HT Case Manager must be able to deliver agency services and initiatives in a culturally sensitive manner specific to the person’s race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, disability, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression.

The HT Case Manager works as a member of the Human Trafficking team to provide services to shelter, transitional housing, and community-based clients. The HT Case Manager reports directly to the Director of Human Trafficking Services.

Key Responsibilities:

Client Services

Conducts intake sessions with new residents in the program.
Works with clients to develop, implement, and maintain individualized case plans and working care plans for residents.
Provides regular case management and access to in-agency and external resources for shelter, transitional housing, and adult community clients.
Works closely with referring agencies, including but not limited to victim witness and the criminal justice system, on behalf of clients.
Transports and accompanies clients to appointments and court as needed; ensures agency van maintenance and upkeep.
Refers clients to other agencies and resources and advocates directly with other agencies as needed to help clients access necessary services.
Provides client-centered crisis intervention, risk assessment, supportive counseling, and safety planning.
Educates clients about the dynamics of human trafficking, sexual assault, and substance abuse.
Facilitates regular house meetings at shelter and transitional housing locations.
Facilitates psychoeducational groups, including but not limited to: WCR (Wellness, Connection, & Resiliency) Group, Seeking Safety Group, Community Group
Maintains strong communication with counseling and shelter team staff regarding client cases.
Performs routine drug and alcohol screening for clients.
Serves as part of the on-call team for the HT Shelter, along with other HT Leadership and the Director of Human Trafficking Services, to assist in emergency situations.

Program & Facility Responsibilities

Oversees maintenance coordination and general upkeep of HT emergency shelter and HT transitional houses to ensure safe and supportive living environments.
Ensures agency vehicle (van) maintenance, including scheduling services and maintaining cleanliness and readiness for client transportation.
Supervises interns and oversees the Human Trafficking intern program, including training, mentorship, and performance support.

Administrative Duties

Completes documentation of case management sessions and group facilitation.
Maintains strict confidentiality of client information in accordance with agency policies, funder requirements, and applicable federal and state laws.
Maintains client outcome database and prepares reports as needed.
Represents Safe Harbor at designated meetings and community collaborations.
EmpowerNet Meeting
Richmond Regional Human Trafficking Collaborative
Participates in regular supervision with the Director of Human Trafficking Services.
Participates in weekly team meetings and monthly staff meetings.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Team Member Expectations

Demonstrates commitment to agency mission.
Demonstrates knowledge of and adherence to agency core values and staff governing values.
Attends all required agency meetings and events.
Participates in regular training to enhance knowledge and skills, per accreditation criteria.
Assists other staff members on projects as needed.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in related field and/or five years of advocacy experience, preferred.
Strong organizational skills and experience managing multiple projects.
Experience using Microsoft Office software platforms.
Ability to communicate both orally and in writing with team members and clients.
Demonstrated understanding of sexual abuse and substance abuse.
Experience facilitating psychoeducational or therapeutic groups preferred.
Experience supervising interns or volunteers preferred.
Must work well with persons of varied sexual preference, racial, ethnic, cultural, socioeconomic backgrounds, and with individuals who are differently-abled.
Previous employment or volunteer work in human services, community agencies, or other related nonprofit or social change organizations a plus.
Ability to remain patient, calm, and professional when working in crisis situations, and able to make decisions independently and as a member of a team.
Required to work occasional evenings, weekends, and holiday hours.

Location
: 3425 S Clarkson St, Englewood, CO 80113. This position requires in-office attendance.

Mon-Fri 8AM-4:30PM.

$36.58 / Hour - $50.64 / Hour.

This position will be posted until Friday 9/4.

Position Summary:

The Quality Management Data Analyst III is a senior-level analytics role responsible for leading complex data analysis, Power BI report development, data validation, and quality reporting initiatives that support hospital operations, regulatory readiness, patient safety, performance improvement, and strategic decision-making. This position partners with Quality, clinical, operational, infection prevention, regulatory, and leadership stakeholders to translate business and clinical questions into reliable data products, clear insights, and governed, sustainable reporting solutions that are maintained throughout their life cycle. The Quality Management Data Analyst III serves as a subject-matter-expert for Microsoft Power BI, SQL-based analysis, data definitions, report modernization, and quality analytics standards, while helping build internal analytics capacity.

Position Requirements:

Licensure/Certification/Registrations: Microsoft Power BI and/or Microsoft Fabric Data Engineer certification preferred.
Education: Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in analytics, data science, information systems, healthcare administration, business, public health, clinical discipline, or related field required.
Experience: Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in data analysis, business intelligence, reporting, or healthcare analytics required. Experience supporting quality, regulatory, patient safety, performance improvement, or hospital operations strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience using SQL to query, validate, reconcile, and assess data integrity across multiple databases required. Advanced experience designing and maintaining Microsoft Power BI reports, dashboards, semantic models, DAX measures, and Power Query transformations required. Experience publishing, troubleshooting, and optimizing governed Power BI reporting solutions required. Experience with dimensional modeling, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Purview, Epic, FHIR, data governance, or healthcare data warehouse environments preferred.
Skills & Abilities: Advanced analytical, technical, communication, and project management skills. Ability to independently lead complex analytics projects from requirements gathering through design, validation, deployment, adoption, and ongoing maintenance. Strong understanding of data quality, metric definitions, regulatory reporting, confidentiality, HIPAA-sensitive data handling, and stakeholder communication. Ability to explain complex technical concepts to clinical, operational, and executive audiences. Ability to manage competing priorities, mentor others, facilitate consensus around data definitions, and maintain a high degree of accuracy, dependability, and attention to detail. Proactively identify reporting gaps and efficiently move projects from intake through adoption with limited direction.

Essential Functions:

Enterprise Analytics and Reporting

Lead the design, development, validation, implementation, and ongoing optimization of enterprise reporting and analytics solutions that support clinical, operational, administrative, financial, regulatory, foundation, and strategic business functions.
Translate complex organizational questions into analytical frameworks, metrics, dashboards, data models, and actionable recommendations that support data-informed decisions at the department, committee, and executive levels.
Independently evaluate and scope analytics requests and recommend priorities in collaboration with leadership and stakeholders, considering organizational value and strategic alignment, regulatory urgency, data readiness, technical feasibility, resource requirements, and long-term supportability.
Use SQL, Power Query, DAX, and related tools to extract, transform, join, reconcile, and validate data from hospital systems, data warehouse environments, foundation or business systems, and other approved data sources.
Develop reporting solutions that balance accuracy, usability, sustainability, performance, confidentiality, and the needs of both technical and non-technical audiences.

Power BI and Microsoft Fabric Leadership

Serve as the hospital's subject-matter-expert for Microsoft Power BI and reporting, including semantic model design, DAX development, data visualization standards, report governance, workspace organization, and report life cycle management.
Support organization-wide implementation, adoption, and effective use of Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric by helping define reporting standards, development practices, access expectations, documentation requirements, and sustainable support models.
Collaborate with data owners and operational stakeholders to align reporting solutions with Microsoft Fabric architecture, approved data sources, data security expectations, and enterprise analytics priorities.
Establish, document, and follow appropriate development, testing, user acceptance, deployment, change-control, and retirement practices for assigned reporting assets, consistent with organizational standards.
Review and improve report logic, semantic models, data refresh processes, measure definitions, dashboard usability, and performance to strengthen trust and consistency in organizational reporting.
Monitor the reliability of assigned production reporting solutions, investigate failures or material discrepancies, communicate impacts to affected stakeholders, and coordinate timely correction and validation.
Evaluate reporting needs and recommend whether solutions should be addressed through enterprise dashboards, departmental Power BI reports, governed semantic models, manual analysis, or other approved reporting approaches.

Data Governance, Data Quality, and Standards

Actively participate in data governance activities, including metric standardization, business glossary development, data cataloging, reporting inventory maintenance, data lineage documentation, stewardship discussions, and validation of approved data definitions.
Establish and maintain clear metric definitions, business rules, calculation logic, source system notes, data lineage, validation evidence, and report documentation to support consistent interpretation across departments and reporting domains.
Identify data discrepancies, investigate root causes, communicate limitations, recommend corrections or process improvements, and verify that changes are implemented appropriately.
Promote responsible data use by applying organizational policies, HIPAA requirements, foundation data stewardship expectations, confidentiality standards, approved access controls, and role-based reporting requirements throughout the analytics life cycle.
Facilitate consensus among stakeholders when definitions, data sources, business rules, or reporting expectations differ across departments.

Training, Consultation, and Data Literacy

Develop and maintain training materials, quick reference guides, report documentation, office hours, and user support resources that improve Power BI adoption, reporting literacy, and consistent interpretation of dashboards across the hospital.
Design and deliver education sessions, demonstrations, and consultative support for leaders, clinicians, administrative teams, foundation staff, analysts, fellows, interns, and departmental report developers.
Coach colleagues on dashboard navigation, appropriate use of measures, interpretation of trends and variation, limitations of available data, and responsible use of self-service reporting tools.
Mentor analysts and project contributors on report development practices, data validation methods, documentation expectations, visualization design, and analytics problem-solving.
Serve as a consultative partner for departments seeking to modernize reports, clarify metrics, improve reporting workflows, or increase local data literacy.

Strategic Partnership and Organizational Support

Partner with executive, clinical, operational, administrative, and foundation leaders to identify strategic reporting opportunities and translate organizational priorities into reliable analytics solutions.
Support multidisciplinary committees, project teams, regulatory readiness efforts, operational improvement initiatives, foundation reporting priorities, and enterprise analytics projects through timely and actionable analysis.
Evaluate report adoption, usability, stakeholder understanding, and ongoing business value, and use feedback to improve reporting products, training, and support approaches.
Provide clear written and verbal explanations of findings, assumptions, limitations, risks, and recommendations to audiences with varying levels of technical expertise.
Maintain current knowledge of healthcare analytics, business intelligence, Microsoft Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, data governance, federal and state requirements, accreditation standards, and emerging reporting practices relevant to the organization.

Job Title: Healthcare Entry to Intermediate Professional (Care Coordinator)

Job Summary:

The PROMISE Clinic, an integrated behavioral health program that supports pregnant and postpartum patients as part of their prenatal care at UCHealth Anschutz, has an opening for a full-time Care Coordinator (Healthcare Entry to Intermediate Professional). This position primarily supports patients experiencing mental health symptoms by improving access to care and coordinating services through referral management, appointment scheduling, patient outreach, and assistance navigating PROMISE and other behavioral health services. The Care Coordinator also supports essential program operations, including maintaining patient and referral data, developing relationships with referring providers, and assisting with clinical data collection and reporting.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as a primary point of contact for PROMISE patients, supporting referrals, scheduling, forms, resources, and access to services.
Manage referrals from receipt through scheduling and connection with care, including follow-up with patients and referring providers.
Provide patients with PROMISE and community resource information and schedule and reschedule appointments in Epic and conduct outreach regarding referrals, missed visits, and incomplete paperwork.
Document referral and care-coordination encounters in accordance with program and institutional requirements.
Maintain patient confidentiality and promptly route clinical questions, safety concerns, medication questions, and treatment requests to licensed clinicians.
Maintain relationships with referral sources and support outreach to referring practices and community partners, accurate referral, census, scheduling, and care-coordination data in Epic, REDCap, Excel, and other approved systems.
Track key patient and program metrics, including census, six-month postpartum status, and patients needing clinician review for discharge and collect and compile clinical and program data for grant reporting, productivity, evaluation, quality improvement, and planning.
Work with program leaders, providers, and staff to support daily operations and process improvement and provide administrative and operational support for PROMISE program activities and team functions.

Work Location:

Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in Aurora, CO.

Why Join Us:

The University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus is a world-class medical destination at the forefront of transformative science, medicine, education and patient care. The campus encompasses the University of Colorado health professional schools, more than 60 centers and institutes, and two nationally ranked independent hospitals - UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital and Children's Hospital Colorado - that treat more than two million adult and pediatric patients each year. Innovative, interconnected and highly collaborative, the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus delivers life-changing treatments, patient care and professional training and conducts world-renowned research fueled by over $650 million in research grants. For more information, visit www.cuanschutz.edu.

The Department of Psychiatry is one of the largest units in the UCD-SOM and is comprised of 5 Divisions. The CU Department of Psychiatry sets the standard for Education and Training of leaders in psychiatry and mental health care, conducts ground-breaking Research that aims to eradicate suffering due to psychiatric and substance use disorders, provides ready access to state of-the-art mental health preventions and interventions across the continuum of care, and collaborates with the community and other key stakeholders to promote well-being among all Coloradans. We accomplish this vision in a manner that respects, values and advocates for the dignity and worth of each individual and family.

The PROMISE Clinic is an integrated behavioral health program at UCHealth Anschutz that supports pregnant and postpartum patients as part of their prenatal and postpartum care. PROMISE provides timely access to behavioral health services through close collaboration among patients, obstetric providers, and mental health providers. The program focuses on identifying mental health needs, connecting patients with appropriate services and resources, coordinating referrals and follow-up, and supporting continuity of care throughout the perinatal period. PROMISE serves a diverse, high-needs patient population, including individuals facing complex behavioral health, medical, social, and access-to-care challenges during pregnancy and the postpartum period.

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

ECO Pass: Reduced rate RTD Bus and light rail service

There are many additional perks & programs with the CU Advantage.

Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Counseling, Social Work, Public Health, or related field from an accredited institution

Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Counseling, Social Work, Public Health, or related field from an accredited institution

Documents in patient’s electronic data base ongoing communication with all individuals responsible for the continuum of care or regulatory issues.
Demonstrates the ability to use the various computer programs required.

jobs.description:
Mission Statement

Michigan Medicine improves the health of patients, populations and communities through excellence in education, patient care, community service, research and technology development, and through leadership activities in Michigan, nationally and internationally. Our mission is guided by our Strategic Principles and has three critical components; patient care, education and research that together enhance our contribution to society.

Job Summary

The Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the Von Voigtlander Women?s Clinic provides consultation, comprehensive treatment and a broad range of services and procedures for patients with normal and high-risk pregnancies and for a broad range of gynecologic services. The clinic team includes physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, medical assistants, social workers, dieticians, as well as a multifunctional administrative/clerical team.

Responsibilities*

Provide culturally sensitive, age-specific nursing care within a team-based care model to patients seen at the Von Voigtlander OBGYN clinic.
Provide the delivery of culturally sensitive, age-specific team-based care models in delivering nursing care for primary Care patients including, adult medicine, pediatric, and OB/GYN patient populations.
Perform phone triage, referral tirage, including assessment, screening, clinical advice, nurse visits (in person/virtual/phone visits), in-clinic hands on procedures, and other duties assigned.
Accurate and efficient documentation of nursing care.
Knowledge and appropriate use of internal and external resources.
Provide functional supervision to assistive personnel; collaborate with colleagues, other disciplines, and health care/community services to promote continuity of care.
Clinical duties include:
Use clinical knowledge and reasoning, and critical thinking to assess and evaluate the needs of OBGYN and Maternal Fetal Medicine (MFM) patients.
Work collaboratively with physicians, advanced practice providers, and ancillary services to provide high quality effective patient care.
Direct outpatient clinical support through InBasket messages and telephone triage supporting a seamless delivery of care.
Participate in the coordination of care, including medication management, placing orders per protocol, relaying test results, completing OB intakes and post op calls, providing patient and family education, managing emergency situations that arise in clinic, and other clinical tasks and indicated.
Document care and patient progress through detailed patient records.
Provide direct patient care within the ambulatory setting, including, but not limited to, patient assessment, patient/family education and counseling and support based on the nursing process and within role/scope of practice.
Coordinate and manage the care of the gynecological, obstetrical, and maternal fetal medicine patients in collaboration with the health care team, including coordinating appointments, monitoring test and lab results, providing patient education and assessment.
Collaborate with care team to develop and provide education for patients, and to the nursing staff, students, fellows, residents, and the community.
Perform preliminary assessment of patients through observation and chart review to facilitate appropriate follow-up with the healthcare team.
Maintain complete and accurate patient charts including chart preparation prior to the patient?s visit.
Evaluate unstable or complex patient care situations and facilitates appropriate interventions and referrals.
Implement appropriate clinical decisions and accept accountability of care provided by self and by healthcare providers to who care is delegated.
Collaborate with and serve as a resource to the clinical team, including social workers, OBGYN nurses, clerical team, and physicians regarding patient care.
Evaluate effectiveness of patient and family teaching
Respond to patient treatment-related phone calls and inbasket messages.
Assist physicians with clinical activities and medical procedures, as needed.
Supporting clinical and translational research.
Attending and participating in conferences and continuing education/staff development programs to maintain knowledge of current literature. Provide functional supervision to assistive personnel; collaborate with colleagues, other disciplines, and health care/community services to promote continuity of care.
Other nursing duties as assigned.

Expectations
Demonstrated critical thinking skills through use of the nursing process, excellent problem-solving skills, and demonstrated ability to set priorities.
Demonstrated customer service, interpersonal communication skills, and the ability to build respectful relationships within and between units and individuals.
Demonstrated accountability and dependability including a good attendance record with punctuality.
Demonstrated adaptability to changing needs and priorities based on unit, department, and institutional goals/objectives.
Demonstrated knowledge and skills providing patient and family education and coaching related to chronic conditions including, but not limited to, diabetes, asthma, and coronary artery disease.
Proficiency with typing and electronic health record documentation.
Ability to manage complex clinical issues utilizing assessment skills, protocols, and evidence-based interventions.
Willingness to adapt to different populations ie: pediatrics, OB/GYN, adult medicine as patient demands.
Demonstrated accountability and dependability for example, completion of work, mandatories, and goal setting within established timelines.

Required Qualifications*

Current license to practice as a registered nurse in the State of Michigan
Required Educational Requirement; applicant must meet one of the following:

NOTE: Required qualifications must be met by the candidate in order to be interviewed and considered for the position.

Bachelors degree in nursing OR
Associate degree or diploma in Nursing and a Masters degree or higher in Nursing
Minimum of three (3) years recent (within the last seven (7) years) experience in Labor and Delivery
Minimum of two (2) years of experience within an ambulatory care clinic
BLS certification

RESUME REQUIRED (for Both Internal & External Applicants)

You must attach a complete and accurate resume to be fully considered for this position.

Desired Qualifications*

Three (3) year of ambulatory care experience within OBGYN
One (1) year of Maternal Fetal Medicine ambulatory care experience
Greater than five (5) years of OBGYN experience.
One (1) year of additional specialty GYN ambulatory care experience in Vulvar, Peds GYN, Transgender Patients, Minimally Invasive Surgery, and Chronic Pelvic Pain
Previous experience using clinical protocols to make decisions for adult patients and facilitating education staff when new protocols are developed or modified.
Experience with MiChart, EPIC, Cisco Finesse, Word, and Excel
Minimum of one (1) year recent (within the last seven (7) years) experience in OBGYN or labor and delivery patient triage
Certification in Ambulatory Nursing
Certification in Obstetric Nursing

Michigan Medicine is one of the largest health care complexes in the world and has been the site of many groundbreaking medical and technological advancements since the opening of the U-M Medical School in 1850. Michigan Medicine is comprised of over 26,000 employees and our vision is to attract, inspire, and develop outstanding people in medicine, sciences, and healthcare to become one of the worlds most distinguished academic health systems. In some way, great or small, every person here helps to advance this world-class institution. Work at Michigan Medicine and become a victor for the greater good.

Location: New Castle, DE 19720

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Behavioral Health Case Manager II (BHCM II) to provide professional behavioral health case management services in a psychiatric outpatient setting. The BHCM II will work with individuals who have developmental disabilities, mental illness, or emotional disorders to help them achieve greater social, emotional, economic, and physical stability and personal independence.
The ideal candidate will have strong experience in behavioral health, social work, case management, assessment, treatment planning, counseling, and coordination of services.

Key Responsibilities

Provide comprehensive behavioral health case management services in a psychiatric outpatient setting.
Conduct client assessments and identify individual behavioral health and human service needs.
Develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate individualized treatment and service plans.
Provide person-centered services designed to promote independence and stability.
Coordinate services and resources for individuals with mental illness, developmental disabilities, or emotional disorders.
Provide counseling, interviewing, and supportive services to clients.
Monitor client progress and make appropriate adjustments to treatment or service plans.
Assess and manage client risk and safety concerns.
Coordinate referrals to appropriate social service agencies and community resources.
Collaborate with treatment teams, healthcare providers, state agencies, and private organizations.
Provide consultative services to other state and private agencies as appropriate.
Maintain accurate and timely case documentation and records.
Support comprehensive patient care while maintaining the integrity of Delaware's behavioral health services.

Master's degree in Behavioral Science, Social Science, Social Work, or a related field.
Three years of case management experience, including:
Assessing client needs
Treatment/service planning
Developing and implementing service plans
Monitoring and evaluating services
Using counseling or interviewing techniques
Connecting clients with appropriate resources

Three years of experience providing clinical treatment or counseling, or determining eligibility for services or benefits as part of a treatment team.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a psychiatric, behavioral health, or outpatient mental health setting.
Experience working with individuals with mental illness, developmental disabilities, or emotional disorders.
Knowledge of behavioral health case management practices and community resources.
Strong assessment, documentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary treatment teams.
Strong understanding of person-centered care and client safety/risk management.

jobs.title: Foster Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Foster Program Coordinator 

Schedule: 

The working schedule for this position is Tuesday - Saturday, 9:30AM - 6PM with Sunday and Monday day off.

Who We Are

ACC is one of the nation’s largest open-admission animal shelters, whose mission is to End Animal Homelessness in NYC. We touch the lives of nearly 30,000 animals each year. ACC is more than an animal shelter; we are a resource to the community, always seeking ways to keep the human-animal bond intact. With a 90% placement rate, our progressive, life-saving initiatives contribute to the successful placement of our animals. 

We strive to find loving homes for homeless and abandoned cats, dogs, guinea pigs and rabbits, both by adopting animals directly to the public and by partnering with more than 200 dedicated animal placement organizations (our New Hope partners). We also help keep NYC communities safe and rescue animals in need, responding to emergencies that involve animals as well as keeping our doors open 24/7 for people and animals in need.

Summary

The Foster Program Coordinator is responsible for maintaining the day-to-day operations of the foster program. As a Foster Program Coordinator, you will be responsible for coordinating the movement of animals in and out of foster homes, providing support to a network of over 800 foster parents, and help facilitate the adoption process for every animal in foster care. 

Required Qualifications
:

High School Diploma or GED required.

The ideal candidate should have a minimum of two-years work experience in a client facing position.

Strong computer literacy required.

Able to excel in a fast-paced, often high-stress, ever-changing environment.  

Treat animals and people with respect and employ humane handling techniques whenever possible. 

Must be able to lift and move up to 50 lbs.

Benefits

ACC values work/life balance and offers a generous paid-time-off (PTO) package that includes vacation time, birthdays off, personal days and sick pay. We also value physical and mental health by offering a great open access Cigna medical, dental and vision insurance at a low premium to our employees as well as 401K and Pension, Life Insurance. We also have on-the-job training for 2-4 weeks, periodic all staff trainings to include safety, DEI, cross training, and other growth opportunities. 

Because ACC is a nonprofit, employees may be eligible for loan forgiveness, cancellation, and/or consolidation under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program (PSLF). Created under the College Cost Reduction and Access Act of 2007, PSLF allows borrowers who work full time for nonprofits and government agencies to have their outstanding debt forgiven tax-free on Federal Direct Loans, after making 120 qualifying monthly payments under a qualifying repayment plan.

Please use this link for more details on our benefits package.

Essential Job Functions
:

Provide support to foster volunteers to ensure all their needs are being met. This includes answering questions, providing support for behavioral issues, following up with medical concerns, and handling other issues that may arise.

Coordinate transportation of foster animals to foster volunteers, between care centers, and to adoption events.

Coordinate with Veterinary Services to ensure foster animals leave the care center with appropriate vaccines and treatment plans, schedule follow-up vet appointments, and assist with handling animals when appropriate.

Other Responsibilities
:

Assist in identifying appropriate foster animals for off-site adoption, outreach, and media opportunities. 

Coordinate logistics for foster animals attending events including scheduling behavior assessments, medical, and transport.

Assist Foster Supervisor with management of foster volunteer database.

Secure appropriate photographs of animals for foster and events.

Recruit new foster volunteers through orientations, interviews, and training.

Lead Open Foster Hours, identify appropriate foster animals to new fosters. 

Fear Free certification within 30 days of hire. 

Complete other duties as assigned by supervisor.

Preferred Qualifications
:

Bachelor’s degree preferred.

Prior experience with Microsoft Office Suite preferred.

Prior experience with animals (dogs/cats/rabbits), either paid or volunteer, is strongly preferred but not required.

Bi-lingual (Spanish) preferred but not required.

Customer-driven and focused on providing a positive, upbeat, experience for all clients. 

High attention to detail, strong work ethic, and the ability to thrive while working in busy environment. 

Work well independently but also function seamlessly as a member of a team. 

Work Environment:

At ACC it's all hands-on deck. We work together as a team, which means you may be asked to help with tasks that involve working outside in all sorts of weather. As a busy animal shelter in one of the biggest cities in the world it can get noisy inside. Employees should have the ability to remain calm yet professional in stressful situations involving animals and/or members of the public. ACC houses hundreds of animals in its facilities at any given time and with that comes fur, odors and other airborne particles in abundance. 

ACC offers many low-cost services to pets and people in need. This includes compassionate end-of-life services for people who cannot afford to go to a private veterinary office but still want to provide a professional and peaceful transition for their beloved pet. 

Training will take place at our Manhattan Centers. Employees will report there until the Bronx location is fully operational.

Reports To:
Foster Supervisor

Overtime: 
This is a non-union position and is eligible for overtime.

Job Description

Our Commitment

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experiences. Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service.

Who we are

As one of the fastest-growing academic health centers in the nation, Texas A&M Health encompasses five colleges and numerous centers and institutes working together to improve health through transformative education, innovative research and team-based health care delivery.

What we want

The Program Coordinator II, in partnership with the residency program director, coordinates and manages the daily activities of the Psychiatry Residency at Texas A&M. Provides curriculum delivery coordination, office management, continuous accreditation readiness, and personnel management. Serves as a liaison to program administrators, residents, faculty, and associated staff of the School of Medicine. Performs many aspects of resident and faculty recruitment, alumni relations, and promotion of the department’s comprehensive educational mission.

Responsibilities:

Program coordination, administration, and oversight

Coordinates and administers the psychiatry residency program, including creating and maintaining resident training files within various online repositories in accordance with the rules and standards established by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME), the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN), Texas Medical Board (TMB), and other oversight bodies.
Oversees a coordinated system of faculty and resident scheduling to ensure achievement of educational objectives which complement the effective operation of a clinical enterprise while ensuring compliance with all applicable accreditation standards.
Implements a system of effective and efficient resident recruitment, interviewing, and onboarding.
May supervise office and administrative support staff in support of the program’s educational mission.
Assists in establishing short- and long-term goals, objectives and strategic plans.
Collaborates with others to create new and expanded programs.
Plans, implements, and evaluates programs.
Assists in establishing policies and procedures.
Prepares reports on program activities.

Learning Management System Administration

Serves as the program’s primary administrator of the New Innovations residency management software suite.
Coordinates the use of residency management tools within the software system and develop and deliver training to faculty and resident users.
Utilizes the learning management system to coordinate and oversee program management activities including scheduling, duty hours compliance, and resident/fellow evaluation completion.
Utilizes the New Innovations suite as the department’s primary repository for trainee files.

Business processes, administrative management, and regulatory affairs

Assists the School of Medicine in managing finances of the residency program, as necessary, in conjunction with the School’s Business and GME Offices.
Assists GME leadership at Texas A&M with administrative responsibilities related to maintenance of all Affiliation Agreements between participating sites and the sponsoring institution, Program Letters of Agreement between programs and rotation sites, and other agreements as necessary.
Oversees processes relating to resident and faculty licensure, certifications, and other regulatory affairs as required by Texas A&M Health and affiliate teaching sites.
Coordinates, develops, evaluates, and ensures adherence to office procedures to eliminate duplication of effort and streamline flow of operations.
Ensures compliance with Texas A&M University and affiliate clinical teaching sites’ administrative policies and procedures.

Accreditation Coordination

Creates a system of continuous accreditation readiness which supports the efforts of the department, program director, and GME Office to comply with the requirements and mandates set forth by the Accreditation Council of Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) and Liaison Committee for Medical Education (LCME).
Develops and implements processes which facilitate an effective Program Evaluation Committee (PEC) and Clinical Competency Committee (CCC).

Program Marketing and communication

Manages program website and both internal and external communications.
Maintains effective communication with community partners, affiliate health systems, and alumni.
Coordinates faculty and resident recruitment efforts to include participation in on- and off-site recruitment events, development of marketing materials, and overall departmental promotion.

Special events coordination

Executes and coordinates logistics for special events and projects including scheduling meetings, booking locations, assisting with transportation and lodging reservations, overseeing and managing event budgets, catering, and compiling meeting materials. Such events include but are not limited to graduation ceremonies, white coat events, and on-site recruitment activities
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Four years of residency program, medical education, or undergraduate education program coordination experience

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree
Five years of residency program or medical education program coordination experience; psychiatry or behavioral health program experience
Current certification from Training Administrators for Graduate Medical Education (C-TAGME)
Knowledge of and experience in instructional design and/or curriculum development
Recent experience with ACGME institutional or program site visits and CLER consultative visits.
Experience working with learning management systems including New Innovations.

Knowledge Skills & Abilities:

Knowledge of word processing, spreadsheet, and database applications.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to perform all tasks and job responsibilities safely without injury to self and others in compliance with A&M System and HSC guidelines.
Ability to multi-task and work cooperatively with others.
Knowledge and experience with event planning and/or project management

Why Texas A&M University?

We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration.  Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you.  Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes. 

Medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life and AD&D, flexible spending accounts, and long-term disability insurance with Texas A&M contributing to employee health and basic life premiums

jobs.title: South Everett Program Manager
jobs.description:
Snotrac is seeking a South Everett Program Manager to lead the "A Safer South Everett" community-driven visioning and mobility planning project. Funded by the Sandy Williams Connecting Communities Grant under the Climate Commitment Act, this initiative runs from August 2026 through December 2027. The Manager will focus heavily on the Evergreen Way corridor between 75th Street and 100th Street. A core objective of this role is to elevate the voices of immigrant, refugee, low-income, transit-dependent, youth, and disabled residents in transportation planning.

Extended Overview

The Snohomish County Transportation Coalition (Snotrac) seeks an energetic, go-getter who is passionate about creating and connecting complete, affordable, age- and ability-friendly communities for all people, especially South Everett.

Snotrac has received a state grant to conduct community engagement in partnership with the City of Everett and Stations Unidos for reimagining Evergreen Way from Airport Road to 41st Street in Everett as a place that is safer and more welcoming for all people, no matter how they get around.  This work will be closely aligned with the City of Everett’s subarea planning for South Everet and parks planning.

This position will lead Snotrac’s community engagement and planning efforts in South Everett related to the Evergreen Way project and other city planning initiatives.

The position will be funded primarily by the state grant, with additional funding from Stations Unidos. Stations Unidos is a community development corporation that supports equitable transit-oriented development and anti-displacement efforts at the future light rail stations of Everett.  The executive director of Snotrac also serves as the CEO of Stations Unidos, and both organizations share an office.

This position is funded by a grant from the Washington State Department of Transportation until December 31, 2027.  Under the grant budget, this position is funded until August 31, 2027 and will terminate at that time.  Additional funding may be sought to sustain this program and position but there is no commitment beyond the initial time-limited period.

Key Responsibilities

Lead monthly coordination meetings with the City of Everett to ensure aligned planning activities, shared surveys, and consistent messaging.
Build meaningful partnerships with trusted community-based organizations, including Stations Unidos, Connect Casino Road, and the Latino Educational Training Institute.
Implement a compensation framework to ensure community members are paid for sharing their lived experiences.
Ensure community input informs the City of Everett's ongoing planning efforts, particularly the new South Everett Subarea Plan.
Conduct extensive direct outreach, including door-to-door engagement at 450 apartments and tabling at 7 local churches, food banks, markets, and transit stops.
Present engagement findings to the City's Evergreen Way Project groups and coordinate closely with the Stations Unidos South Everett Advisory Board.
With Snotrac’s Policy Affairs & Mobility Navigation Program Manager, hire and manage a team of part-time mobility navigators and ambassadors for outreach activities associated with the South Everett initiative.

Community Engagement & Events

Host a variety of feedback forums, including affinity listening sessions, focus groups, youth art workshops, and in-person and online community visioning sessions.
Organize and execute several pop-up park activities
Facilitate community walks and community bicycle rides to conduct active mobility audits.
Organize environmental and mobility justice tabletop game nights.

Additional Activities

Organize and lead the South Everett Advisory Board of Stations Unidos.
Participate in the Real Estate Development Advisory Committee of Stations Unidos.
Participate in the Village Circle meetings.
Monitoring spend-down on the grant.
Grant reporting.
Other duties as assigned, including support of community outreach and engagement efforts across program areas.

Required Deliverables

Develop a comprehensive Engagement Plan, a Decision Point Roadmap, and a Community Vision and Values Framework for Evergreen Way.
Produce community-driven preliminary design concepts for top project elements and an Engagement Summary Report.
Create a Participatory Mapping Dataset and a video-based "Story Book" documenting community experiences with traffic stress, air pollution, and neighborhood aspirations.

Qualifications

Mobility Justice.  Passion
for transit and active transportation as forms of transportation, and for for addressing past injustices to priority populations, including low income individuals and People of Color.
Community Engagement Experience:
Ability to design and lead inclusive community outreach, specifically elevating the voices of immigrant, refugee, low-income, transit-dependent, youth, and disabled populations.
Event Facilitation Skills:
Ability to organize and facilitate a diverse range of events, such as focus groups, interactive workshops, pop-up activities, and listening sessions.
Multilingual Capabilities:
Ability to relate to diverse populations of South Everett and to lead a team of bilingual navigators and ambassadors. Preference for proficiency in Spanish, Russian or other slavic language, Vietnamese, or Tagalog to conduct and coordinate outreach in the language.
Project Management & Coordination:
Strong organizational skills required to manage a multi-phase planning project, maintain timelines, and lead monthly coordination meetings with municipal partners like the City of Everett.
Partnership Building:
Experience building and maintaining meaningful, trust-based relationships with community-based organizations and local stakeholders.
Active Mobility Comfort:
Willingness and ability to lead and participate in on-the-ground community walks and bicycle rides to conduct active transportation audits.  Applicant must also enjoy and proficiently play a range of tabletop games.
Relationship Building:
Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with a wide range of community members, specifically Spanish-speaking mothers for community walks and young adults and youth for community bike rides.
Familiarity with South Everett:
Existing connections with local organizations in the Casino Road and Evergreen Way corridors, such as Stations Unidos, Connect Casino Road, or the Latino Educational Training Institute. Residence in or near South Everett is preferred.
Transportation Planning Knowledge:
Background in transportation planning, mobility justice, and "Complete Streets" initiatives, with an understanding of how to integrate community recommendations into municipal subarea plans.
Land Use and Real Estate Planning Knowledge:
Background in urban planning and real estate development.
Data & Storytelling Experience:
Experience capturing qualitative and quantitative data, specifically through participatory mapping datasets and video-based community storytelling.
Equitable Compensation Management:
Previous experience developing or administering compensation frameworks to equitably pay community members for their lived experience and participation.
Team Management:
Ability to lead a bilingual team of navigators and ambassadors.
Physical Requirements:
Ability to lift 50 lbs and ride a bicycle, necessary for setting up the pop-up park activities and leading the bicycle rides.

Background Checks

Because Snotrac works with youth, people with disabilities, and older adults, Snotrac screens potential employees for crimes against children, sexual assaults, other crimes, and motor vehicle violations.

Reports to:
Executive Director

Location:
Hybrid: weekly in-person check-in meeting at Everett office; frequent in-person activities in South Everett; and work from home as schedule allows.

Equipment:
MS Surface tablet may be provided with necessary software.  Home internet and personal cell phone use may be compensated.

Compensation:

$70,000 - $75,000 per year
Up to $300 per month contribution toward health insurance
Flexible hours
Paid Time Off: federal holidays, accrued sick leave, accrued vacation time.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Snotrac is an equal opportunity employer. We value the importance of creating an environment in which all employees can feel respected, included, and empowered to bring unique ideas to the organization. Our diversity and inclusion efforts include embracing different cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints while fostering growth and advancement in the workplace. 

To Apply 

Submit cover letter and resume by email to Brock Howell, Executive Director, at brock@snotrac.org; indicate “South Everett Program Manager” in the subject line.
No phone calls please. 
Position open until filled. Applications will be reviewed as submitted.

A cover letter is required for consideration for this position and should be attached as the first page of your resume. The cover letter should address your specific interest in the position and outline skills and experience that directly relate to this position.

Job Summary

Department Summary:

Michigan Housing is an actively engaged unit within Student Life Auxiliary Services within the Division of Student Life. M Housing serves approximately 11,500 students: 9,100 undergraduate and 2,400 graduate and professional students and their families. Although first-year students are not required to live on campus, historically 96-98% of all new first-year students choose to live on. Currently, the M Housing portfolio consists of 19 residential facilities that include traditional residence halls, apartments, and other living options located in communities on north and central campuses in Ann Arbor. In partnership with Michigan Dining, there are 9 dining halls and 9 retail operations embedded within the residence halls that serve approximately 4 million meals per year. Beginning Fall 2024, M Housing partnered with other units and departments within Student Life to support the residential experience for approximately 25 U-M students on the Marygrove campus, located in Detroit. In Fall 2026, five new residence halls housing 2,300 undergraduate students and a new 822-seat dining facility will open to continue M Housing's strong tradition of providing affordable housing options and services for U-M students. In addition to supporting the academic mission of the University, M Housing creates and sustains diverse learning-centered residential communities that ultimately enhance the residential experience.

The University of Michigan Lawyers Club is a 501C3 with a MOU with Michigan Housing and the University of Michigan. It serves as a residence for law students, an event and gathering space for the legal education community, and serves Michigan Law students, faculty, alumni, and guests. The Lawyers Club contains residential spaces with contract holders, guestrooms for overnight guests, and a dining facility. The Club works in tandem with various law school departments, including admissions, development and alumni relations, faculty teaching, student life, and the first-year program.

The Lawyers Club Program Manager has day-to-day responsibility for the administrative, engagement, and resident support functions of the Lawyers Club in coordination with the Assistant Director for Academic Initiatives. The Lawyer's Club Program Manager aligns their work with the policies and procedures of Michigan Housing in concert with the requirements of a world-class professional school, which operates under the American Bar Association specifications. The Lawyers Club is an integral part of Michigan Law in providing outside-of-the-classroom experiences to current and future students, alumni, and guests.

Collaborate with University of Michigan Law School and campus partners to facilitate events hosted in the Lawyers Club.
