jobs.description:
Background

Bloomberg Philanthropies works to create catalytic change across five areas of focus: arts and culture, education, the environment, government innovation, and public health. Our mission is to ensure better, longer lives for the greatest number of people. Our approach is rooted in Mike Bloomberg’s unique experience and success across business, government, and philanthropy.

The Government Innovation
programs build the capacity of local governments to solve problems effectively. Its initiatives – ranging from large-scale international innovation competitions to domestic efforts that help mayors hone their management skills and better use data in decision-making – equip local leaders with practical tools and approaches they can use to address local challenges. We currently invest in municipal governments worldwide through grants, technical assistance, and participation programs. Our team is collegial and collaborative with an orientation toward learning at the individual, group, and portfolio levels. We are energized to advance our mission, while also working to ensure team members have full and balanced lives and opportunities for growth.

The Position

The Ideas
Initiatives
,
including initiatives like the Bloomberg Mayors Challenge
and Bloomberg Cities Idea Exchange,
identifies and grows promising ideas that help city governments solve their most pressing challenges. We support cities in generating ambitious solutions, adapting proven approaches, and accelerating the spread of ideas that improve residents’ lives. The Program Manager
will support the delivery and continued development of the Ideas Initiatives, including future initiatives that identify, develop, test, grow, and spread promising ideas for city governments.

The role is based in New York City and will require occasional domestic and international travel.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Delivery & Partner Management
Manage day-to-day delivery of key components of the Bloomberg Mayors Challenge, Bloomberg Cities Idea Exchange, and related initiatives. As an example, delivering key components of the Bloomberg Mayors Challenge competition, including developing the application, review, evaluation, selection and event processes.
Serve as a relationship manager for external partners delivering major components of the portfolio, providing strategic guidance, candid feedback, and ongoing problem-solving support.
Monitor partner performance, deliverables, milestones, budgets, and risks across multiple initiatives, ensuring work meets Bloomberg Philanthropies’ standards.
Support the planning and execution of workshops, convenings, site visits, and other program activities involving cities, partners, and external stakeholders.

Ideas Development & Evidence Building
Manage key components of idea evaluation across idea initiatives, including coordinating partner-led evaluations of select Bloomberg Mayors Challenge-supported ideas and overseeing the Bloomberg Cities Idea Exchange idea evaluation fund.
Supporting the sourcing and initial assessment of promising city-led ideas with the potential to improve outcomes for residents and be adopted by other cities.
Synthesize research, evaluation, and learning activities that strengthen the evidence base for supported ideas and inform decisions about further investment or expansion.

Portfolio Operations & Project Management
Design, maintain, and continuously improve dashboards, trackers, workflows, templates, and other portfolio management tools.
Coordinate integrated project plans, timelines, budgets, dependencies, and cross-team workflows across multiple initiatives.
Provide day-to-day operational support across initiatives by maintaining files and trackers, documenting decisions and action items, processing contracts and invoicing, and periodically supporting meeting coordination.

Strategic Projects & Internal Initiative Learning
Draft memos, briefing documents, presentations, and recommendations for Bloomberg Philanthropies leadership.
Prepare program summaries, reports, talking points, and other communications that translate initiative activity and results into clear insights for institutional decision-making.
Conduct research and synthesize lessons from programs, partners, cities, and external sources to strengthen existing initiatives and inform future program design.
Monitor emerging trends and developments in public innovation, civic technology, implementation, and city government.

Qualifications Of The Ideal Candidate

8+ years of relevant, full-time professional experience. We recognize there are many paths to this role and welcome candidates from government, philanthropy, consulting, product development, design, venture investing, startups, civic technology, entrepreneurship, applied research, or other fields where they have helped develop, test, or grow new ideas. Experience working with or alongside city governments is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience designing and implementing complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives from strategy through execution.
Excellent project management and organizational skills, with experience managing multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complexity into clear, compelling narratives, presentations, and decision documents.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an ability to connect day-to-day program work to broader organizational goals.
Exceptional interpersonal and relationship management skills, with a track record of building and managing partnerships across governments, nonprofits, philanthropy, and other external partners.
Intellectual curiosity about how innovation happens inside and outside government, and enthusiasm for applying ideas from adjacent fields to improve how cities solve problems.
Adaptable, resourceful, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities evolve.
Strong judgment, high integrity, and the ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and confidentiality.
Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree in public policy, public administration, business, urban planning, design, or a related field preferred.

JOB TITLE

Program Coordinator

LOCATION

Worcester

DEPARTMENT NAME

Robotics Engineering

DIVISION NAME

Worcester Polytechnic Institute - WPI

Job Description Summary

Worcester Polytechnic Institute seeks a full-time Program Coordinator for a six-year, NSF-funded S-STEM scholarship program that will support 70 annual scholarships for low-income undergraduate and master's students across four degree programs (RBE, MME, CEAE, IMGD). The program combines scholarships with an integrated set of academic and professional development activities: VINE (Vertically Integrated Nexus Experience) research projects that connect scholars across academic levels, CoHORT cross-disciplinary project teams organized around convergent research themes, a personalized Bridge curriculum for transfer and entering scholars, and a structured internship and career pathway with industry partners.

The Program Coordinator is central to the daily operation and cohort continuity of the program. Working closely with the PI, a Co-PI team spanning four academic programs, an external evaluator, community college partners, and industry partners, the Coordinator serves as the program's operational hub and the primary day-to-day point of contact for scholars. Because scholars enter in overlapping annual cohorts, the position requires someone who can hold a complex, multi-year picture of every participant while running the recurring annual cycle of recruitment, selection, programming, and reporting.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities:

Scholar Recruitment, Selection, and Onboarding

Manage the annual application and selection cycle end to end, including the unified application process, the Spring deadline for fall cohort entry, and the mid-year replacement cycle that maintains full cohort strength.
Work with departmental advisors and Faculty Champions each spring to identify high-potential sophomores eligible for junior-year entry; coordinate with the Office of Student Aid & Financial Literacy to confirm financial eligibility.
Support Faculty Champion follow-up with admitted students prior to enrollment.
Support Co-PI recruiting visits to community college partners (QCC, MWCC, MassBay, NECC, Manchester CC, Berkshire CC, Holyoke CC) and to the University of Puerto Rico–Mayagüez, including scheduling, materials, and follow-up with prospective transfer scholars over the 12–18 month pre-transfer window.
Serve as a member of the selection committee alongside the PI and Co-PIs; administer the holistic review rubric, coordinate faculty recommendation letters, and schedule finalist interviews.
Coordinate onboarding for each incoming cohort, including orientation, Bridge placement, faculty champion assignment, and scholarship award notification.

Cohort Management and Scholar Tracking

Build and maintain the centralized scholar database tracking all participants, with semester-by-semester records of GPA, program participation, financial aid status, and milestone completion.
Monitor early warning indicators (academic, financial, and engagement) and escalate concerns promptly to the PI and the scholar's Faculty Champion so that support can be put in place before a scholar is at risk of leaving.
Track scholarship eligibility, renewal decisions, and award continuation in coordination with the Office of Student Aid & Financial Literacy and the sponsored programs office.
Maintain accurate rosters and status records for scholars moving between stages (junior/senior undergraduate, accelerated BS/MS, master's) and manage the replacement cycle when a scholar exits.

Mentoring and Program Activity Coordination

Coordinate mentor–mentee matching across the program, pairing scholars with near-peer mentors and Faculty Champions based on research theme, discipline, and academic level; monitor Faculty Champion caseloads against the five-scholar cap.
Coordinate scholar placement into VINE vertical projects and CoHORT cross-disciplinary teams, working with faculty to align scholar interests with active projects.
Support delivery of the Bridge curriculum, including coordination of the self-paced module library, the structured summer course pathway for incoming transfer students, and personalized academic plan meetings between scholars, Faculty Champions, and peer mentors.
Plan and execute program events: cohort kickoffs, seminars, workshops, team showcases, industry engagement events, and the annual program meeting. Handle logistics, scheduling, catering, space, and communications.
Coordinate the Scholar Advisory Council and support its members in exercising a genuine student voice in program decisions.

Industry Partnerships and Career Pathways

Serve as the program's liaison with industry partners on internship placements, matching scholars to internal and external opportunities.
Track internship participation and job placement outcomes against program targets.
Coordinate the annual Industry Advisory Board meeting, including scheduling, agenda preparation, materials, and follow-up on internship commitments.
Partner with WPI Career Development Center staff to connect scholars with career services, résumé and interview preparation, and employer events.

Evaluation, Reporting, and Program Administration

Coordinate data collection for the external evaluator, including survey administration, focus group and interview scheduling, consent tracking, and secure transmission of scholar records in accordance with IRB protocols.
Prepare data, tables, and narrative sections for NSF annual and final reports in collaboration with the PI.
Schedule and staff quarterly PI team meetings; prepare agendas, circulate scholar progress and assessment summaries, and track action items to completion.
Monitor programmatic (non-scholarship) budget lines in coordination with the PI and departmental administration; process travel, event, and participant support expenses.
Maintain program communications: website, scholar-facing newsletters and announcements, recruitment materials, and partner-facing updates.
Support dissemination activities, including conference submissions, the practitioner guide, and S-STEM community engagement.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and three or more years of relevant experience in program coordination, student support, academic administration, or grant-funded project management. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
Demonstrated ability to independently manage a recurring program cycle with multiple concurrent deadlines and many participants.
Strong data management skills, including experience building and maintaining participant databases, tracking longitudinal records, and producing accurate reports from them.
Excellent written and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with students, faculty across disciplines, external partners, and administrative offices.
Demonstrated capacity to work with students with discretion, warmth, and sound judgment.
Ability to handle confidential academic and financial records appropriately and in compliance with relevant protocols.
Proficiency with standard productivity and collaboration tools (spreadsheets, databases, survey platforms, shared document systems).

Preferred Qualifications

Higher education administration, STEM education, engineering, or a related field.
Experience coordinating a federally funded education or training program (NSF S-STEM, NRT, REU, RET, LSAMP, or similar), including familiarity with sponsor reporting requirements.
Familiarity with WPI's project-based curriculum (IQP/MQP), accelerated BS/MS pathway, and transfer student infrastructure.
Experience with mentor–mentee matching, cohort programming, or learning community models.
Experience working with community college partners, articulation agreements, or transfer student pathways.
Familiarity with program evaluation practices, IRB processes, and educational research data collection.
Experience coordinating industry relationships or internship placements.
Interest in or exposure to robotics, infrastructure, manufacturing, or interactive media.

Attributes for Success

The strongest candidate for this role is well-organized to run a six-year program on a calendar and relational for scholars to come to them first when something goes wrong. The position rewards someone who notices the quiet student, who keeps a comprehensive database of complex information, and who can move between a spreadsheet of GPA records, a conversation with an industry partner, and a scholar's office-hours drop-in without losing the thread.

Work Environment

Primarily an on-campus office environment. Occasional evening and weekend hours are required around program events, cohort kickoffs, and the annual meeting. Periodic travel to regional community college partners in Massachusetts and New Hampshire is expected; occasional travel to national conferences may be required.

Application

Applicants should submit a cover letter and résumé or CV. The cover letter should describe relevant experience coordinating programs or supporting students, and any experience with grant-funded education programs.

Compensation

$58,500 per year based on related experience, expertise, and internal equity. This position is contingent upon the availability of continue external funding. WPI’s benefits package includes a robust retirement match, wellness perks, tuition assistance and more!

United States of America (Exempt)

All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability. It seeks individuals from all backgrounds and experiences who will contribute to a culture of creativity, collaboration, inclusion, problem solving, innovation, high performance, and change making. It is committed to maintaining a campus environment free of harassment and discrimination.

jobs.title: Grateful Patient Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Job Overview

As Fairview Health Services establishes a new, modern foundation to accelerate its mission, this role serves as a key Fairview Foundation team member contributing towards transformational, multi year, multi million dollar philanthropy program that accelerates Fairview's strategic priorities, including patient care excellence, clinical research and discovery, workforce and physician education, community health, and long-term health system sustainability. The Grateful Patient Program Coordinator builds and executes strategic fundraising initiatives by fostering strategic engagement with grateful patients and families who wish to give back after receiving exceptional care. Serving as a central bridge between foundation leadership, clinical teams, and marketing staff, the coordinator expands the fundraising pipeline across our entire healthcare network. The ideal candidate will balance strategic program growth with day-to-day prospect cultivation, strategic engagement, staff training, and data tracking. This position is relationship-driven and works to create meaningful donor experiences that connect gratitude for care with philanthropic impact. The coordinator supports the development of scalable processes for patient identification, referrals, engagement, and stewardship, ensuring all outreach is professional, empathetic, and compliant with healthcare and donor privacy standards. Strategic Impact

Program Growth: Build and scale a comprehensive grateful patient fundraising program across the Fairview health system.
Pipeline Expansion: Increase the systematic identification, qualification, and strategic engagement of high-potential donor prospects.
Revenue Development: Grow annual and mid-level giving portfolios while strengthening the future major gift pipeline.
Cultural Shift: Foster a culture of philanthropy and mission advancement through generosity and partnership throughout Fairview Health Services.

Responsibilities

Program Development & Implementation
System Rollout: Support the design and rollout of a comprehensive grateful patient fundraising program across the entire Fairview enterprise.
Clinical Pathways: Partner closely with frontline clinical teams to identify and qualify grateful patient prospects, ensuring patient referrals are accurate and timely.
Portfolio Management: Maintain and grow an active portfolio of qualified prospects capable of making annual, mid-level, and future major gifts.
Stewardship Strategies: Working with external and internal stakeholders, develop and execute tailored cultivation strategies for grateful patient prospects, including on-site experiences, structured follow-up, ongoing communication, and long-term donor retention.
Training & Education
Staff Education: Coordinate targeted training sessions for staff, physicians, board members, and clinical leadership.
Best Practices: Lead internal education on grateful patient fundraising best practices, including how to recognize patient expressions of gratitude appropriately. Amplify stories of impact to scale the culture of grateful patient philanthropy and partnership.
Marketing, Collaboration & Data Management
Gift Appeals: Assist in creating compelling gift appeals, marketing materials, and communication strategies focused on themes of gratitude and physician recognition.
Data Integration: Collaborate with data analytics teams to analyze grateful patient records, validate prospective donors, and track referral and engagement metrics.
Cross-Functional Synergy: Partner closely with Fairview Foundation leadership, Fairview Marketing and Communications leadership, Specialty Care and hospital site leadership, and major gift teams to integrate grateful patient fundraising into broader philanthropic strategies.
Compliance & Ethics
Privacy Protections: Ensure all program activities comply with HIPAA regulations, donor policies, and internal healthcare guidelines.
Required Training: Maintain up-to-date knowledge and complete all required annual regulatory compliance training.

Required Qualifications

B.S./B.A. Healthcare Administration, Communications Philanthropy, Business or related field
3 years Professional experience in development, fundraising, or institutional advancement, preferably within a large hospital network or academic medical center.
Experience navigating donor management databases or healthcare CRM software (such as Blackbaud’s Raiser’s Edge NXT) alongside standard spreadsheet tools.
Clear understanding of HIPAA laws regarding the use of patient data for healthcare fundraising purposes.
Exceptional emotional intelligence, active listening, and strong communication skills necessary to collaborate with physicians, corporate leaders, and families navigating complex health journeys.
Highly detail-oriented, with an ability to maneuver in a fast-paced, growth mindset environment.

Benefit Overview

Fairview offers a generous benefit package including but not limited to medical, dental, vision plans, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability insurance, PTO and Sick and Safe Time, tuition reimbursement, retirement, early access to earned wages, and more! Please follow this link foradditional information: https://www.fairview.org/careers/benefits/noncontract

Job Description

We’re hiring a Episodic Care Manager to join the Commercial Utilization Management Team! The Episodic Care Manager is responsible for performing clinical reviews to assess, facilitate, and coordinate the delivery of health care services for members based on medical necessity and contractual benefits. Effectively coordinate with providers, members, and internal staff to support the delivery of high quality and cost-effective care across the health care system.

Clinical Evaluation and Review

Receive assigned cases for varied member services (i.e. inpatient, outpatient, DME)
Review and evaluate cases for medical necessity against medical policy, benefits and/or care guidelines and regulations.
Complete work in accordance with timeliness, production, clinical quality/accuracy and compliance standards
Provide notifications to member and/or provider, according to regulatory requirements.
Assess appropriateness for secondary case review by the Medical Director (MD) for denials and coordinate as needed.
May coordinate peer-to-peer review upon provider request when members’ health conditions do not meet guidelines.

Collaboration and Documentation

Communicate and collaborate effectively with internal and external clinical/non-clinical staff (including MDs) to coordinate work
Appropriately and fully document outcome of reviews and demonstrate the ability to interpret and analyze clinical information
Utilize detailed clinical knowledge to summarize clinical review against the criteria/guidelines to provide necessary information for MDs.

What You Bring

RN with 3 years of clinical experience or LPN with 5 years of clinical experience.
For Behavioral Health specific roles, other applicable licensure may be considered with a minimum of 3 years of clinical experience.
Must have and maintain a valid and applicable clinical license (NC or compact multi-state licensure) to perform described job duties.

Bonus Points (Preferred Qualifications)

Recent hands-on bedside nursing experience in an acute care hospital setting required. Experience may include Medical-Surgical, ICU, Emergency Department, Pediatrics, Labor & Delivery, or other inpatient specialties.
Direct patient care experience and a strong understanding of clinical diagnoses and treatment plans to effectively interpret medical documentation.

What You’ll Get

The opportunity to work at the cutting edge of health care delivery with a team that’s deeply invested in the community 
Work-life balance, flexibility, and the autonomy to do great work 
Medical, dental, and vision coverage along with numerous health and wellness programs 
Parental leave and support plus adoption and surrogacy assistance 
Career development programs and tuition reimbursement for continued education 
401k match including an annual company contribution 
Learn more

Our Hybrid Flex approach is built on presence with a purpose – giving you flexibility to work remotely with intentional in-person connection – that supports a workplace that’s flexible, connected, and future focused.

In a Hybrid-Flex role, you’ll work in the office at least two days a week for collaboration and connection. In a Remote Flex role, you’ll work virtually, with a few in-office visits each year for meaningful moments that matter.

Whether your role is Hybrid Flex or Remote Flex depends on the nature of the work and distance from our Durham headquarters. We welcome candidates from outside the local area and in any states listed on this job posting. Onsite expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

This individual plays a key role in the reporting and process management for Corporate Philanthropy objectives across Middlesex Savings Bank and its Charitable Foundation, with specific focus on sponsorships, scholarships, financial literacy, and grant program support. Along with the Director of Corporate Philanthropy, the Corporate Philanthropy Program Manager handles a portfolio of grants aligned with the Bank and Foundation's priorities including grant evaluation, budget and program goals. The Corporate Philanthropy Program Manager works closely with the Director of Corporate Philanthropy to ensure consistent processes, accurate reporting, and effective systems utilization. The role is responsible for helping to optimize grantmaking, develop dashboards and reporting structures, and create processes that enhance efficiency and visibility of impact.
Responsibilities
Grant Program:

Contribute to internal assessment of grant performance and alignment with Foundation strategy
Serve as first point of contact for grant and charitable inquiries, including sponsorships
Primary relationship owner of the grant database, Blackbaud. Create reports and streamline processes between various programs, with a strong ability in grant analysis and reporting.
Prepare meeting materials, review grant proposals, and provide overall support to the Director of Corporate Philanthropy and Foundation board
Design surveys and improve data collection from grantees
Develop and facilitate virtual informational sessions for prospective applicants
Coordinate feedback meetings for unsuccessful applicants
Support grantee partners in timely completion of reporting requirements
Scholarship Program:

Oversee the scholarship program with area high schools and act as primary liaison with financial partner who facilitates payout of scholarship funds
Maintain relationships with scholarship administrators and guidance departments
Act as point person for all inquiries from scholarship recipients
Sponsorship Program:

Ensure timely coordination of payment, communication and marketing support for all sponsorships
Develop and maintain effective reporting in the Blackbaud database
Provide coordination and support for community events

Coordinate with Marketing team to effectively brand and promote the program
Other:

Work with internal teams to share relevant Board and volunteer opportunities
Other administrative tasks as required to support Corporate Philanthropy and Foundation initiatives

Bachelor's Degree is required

Strong proficiency with database management systems, in particular BlackBaud or similar
High degree of organization, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities
Comfortable working as a self-starter and in a team environment
Ability to represent the Bank in public and community forums
Experience with grants and/or nonprofit program development, a plus
Ability to write professionally and synthesize content.
Position is eligible for a hybrid work schedule, 3 days in the office and 2 days remote following 90 days.

jobs.description:
Job Number: R0247680

Financial Program and Data Analyst

The Opportunity:

As data analyst, you love diving into data and turning it into meaningful insights. With the abundance of structured and unstructured data, you understand the importance of transforming complex data sets into useful information to solve challenges. As a data analyst at Booz Allen, you can use your skills and experience to support a mission and use data for good. We need a data analyst like you to bring your knowledge to complex defense acquisition.

As a client-facing data analyst on our contracting finance team, you’ll work closely with your clients to understand their questions and needs and then dig into their data-rich environments to find the pieces of their information puzzle. Not only will you provide a deep understanding of their data, but you’ll also advise your client on what the information means and how it can be used to make an impact on critical weapon systems to where they are needed the most.

How You’ll Contribute:

As a data analyst on our team, you’ll:

Provide overall acquisition and programmatic expertise and support.
Support annual task planning and allocation reviews.
Provide in-depth financial requirements analysis, draft allocations, performers engagement, task prioritization, funding impacts, and preparation of briefing materials.
Develop funding trackers and perform analysis on execution, expenditures, and expiring funds.
Review performer spend plans, engaging with performers on funding status throughout the year.
Assist with the execution of funding and data calls such as execution reviews and funding deep dives, as requested.
Establish plans for contract actions associated with funding increments and decrements.
Track contract obligation status, funding profiles, and funding requirements.
Perform critical thinking to match up procurement profiles with associated funding plans.
Contribute to effective analysis and management of incoming and outgoing action items assigned from meetings, telecoms, or emails.
Provide meeting support, including agenda support, coordination and facilitation, or tracking actions.
Develop planning models to analyze program health, schedule impacts, and formulate options to best fulfill project requirements.

Work with us to help drive large-scale business and process decisions through data insights.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

2+ years of experience with Power BI or Tableau
2+ years of experience with programming languages such as SQL and Python, for data manipulation and analysis
1+ years of experience with data engineering in Databricks or Spark
Experience with acquisition, program management, and financial analysis, including task planning, allocations, or funding execution with DoW clients such as NAVSEA or NAVWAR
Experience using Microsoft Office 365 Suite applications such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, or SharePoint
Knowledge of Navy systems, including COBRA, ERP, EDW, NEPS, or EVMCR
Ability to be self-motivated and pay strict attention to detail
Secret clearance
Bachelor's degree

Nice If You Have:

Experience with Power Platform, including Power Apps and Power Automate
Experience building or maintaining data pipelines
Knowledge of the Pandas library in Python
Possession of strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, to support reviews, funding actions, and briefing preparation
Possession of strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and critical thinking skills
Databricks or Power BI Certification

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; Secret clearance is required.

Compensation

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $62,000.00 to $141,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date.

Identity Statement

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

Candidate AI Usage Policy

AI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your
own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided
.

Work Model

Our people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration, whether it occurs in person or virtually. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.

Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.
Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen facility frequently, in alignment with leadership expectations and the needs of the role. You may also be required to work from or visit a customer facility.
Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed at a Booz Allen office or customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

We're powering a cleaner, brighter future.

Exelon is leading the energy transformation, and we're calling all problem solvers, innovators, community builders and change makers. Work with us to deliver solutions that make our diverse cities and communities stronger, healthier and more resilient.

We're powered by purpose-driven people like you who believe in being inclusive and creative, and value safety, innovation, integrity and community service. We are a Fortune 200 company, 20,000 colleagues strong serving more than 10.7 million customers at six energy companies -- Atlantic City Electric (ACE), Baltimore Gas and Electric (BGE), Commonwealth Edison (ComEd), Delmarva Power & Light (DPL), PECO Energy Company (PECO), and Potomac Electric Power Company (Pepco).

We're committed to creating an environment where every person can thrive. Our employee experience is grounded in four tenets that guide how we support our people: purposeful careers, growth opportunities, community impact, and support to thrive.

In our relentless pursuit of excellence, we elevate diverse voices, fresh perspectives and bold thinking. And since we know transforming the future of energy is hard work, we provide competitive compensation, incentives, excellent benefits and the opportunity to build a rewarding career.

Are you in?

Primary Purpose

PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION

Develop, implement, and evaluate team projects or programs, including process improvements. Develop business plans, project charters, and performance metrics in support of business objectives. Ensure organizational alignment with management models and principles and drive the integration of best practices. Perform various assignments including requests for financial and operational reports, data analysis and modeling, business planning, and/or performance measurement. Coordinate quality assurance, change management activities and drive safety performance, with both internal and contract personnel. Position may be required to work extended hours for coverage during storms or other energy delivery emergencies.

Primary Duties

PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES

Lead development, implementation, and evaluation of projects, programs, and/or business initiatives. Provide requirements analysis, performance measurement, and quality assurance. Manage scope, schedule, and budget for organizational projects and programs. Perform detailed forecasting and perform invoice reviews on an ongoing basis. (40%)
Understand business processes and provide guidance for end users. Provide day-to-day client support and conduct diagnostics as necessary to ensure optimal performance. Assist and advise other personnel with responses to internal and external inquiries. (15%)
Lead change management activities for projects, programs, and initiatives. Develop and implement training of employees and external personnel for new processes and procedures. Develop and implement effective business readiness procedures. (10%)
Coordinate and report on process/project/initiative assignments. Develop performance indicators and tracking mechanisms to monitor and report results. Prepare, review, and analyze reports, controls, and other financial & operational information for specific projects and initiatives. (10%)
Support the establishment of business plans and objectives across multiple areas / departments. Coordinate with stakeholders on the development of business cases and prioritization of deliverables. (10%)
Participate in process improvement task forces. Provide benchmarking analysis. Prepare status reports to leadership. (5%)
Coordinate work plans to implement corrective actions that are identified as a result of performance assessment. (5%)
Respond to emergent operational issues such as safety incident investigations, outage events, and storm response activity (5%)

Job Scope

JOB SCOPE

Manage ~$2M - $30M programs/projects designated by line item to achieve all program and corporate goals, and mandated requirements. Manage the performance of program/project teams through oversight of 100 to 300 contract field personnel. This includes performing safety observations and incident investigations. Develop and implement innovative strategic initiatives that ensure continued support of capital improvement projects, reliability improvement and cost saving opportunities. Ensure contractor activities are in alignment with all safety and quality expectations as outlined in contract terms & conditions. Interface with internal and external key stakeholders including senior management, customers, governmental and regulatory officials.

Minimum Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in a business or S.T.E.M.-related discipline and 4-7 years field experience OR Associate's degree and 5-6 years field experience, OR HS Diploma and 6-9 years field experience required.
Demonstrated experience leading craft and/or non-craft teams
Demonstrated Program Management skills, writing skills and PC skills including Microsoft Office Suite
Strong interpersonal, communications, customer relations, and presentation skills. Demonstrated experience in public speaking / presenting to a diverse audience
Demonstrated strong budget management skills
Demonstrated experience using critical thinking skills to solve complex problems
Federal, state, and local regulatory and environmental compliance experience
Demonstrated focus on providing premier customer experience with proven written and oral communication skills and ability to interact with people of all levels
Demonstrated business acumen and ability to create value with strong problem solving, analytical/financial, and conflict management skills and a willingness to accept increased responsibilities.

Preferred Qualifications

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Job Summary

Job Description

Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) is seeking a motivated Research Assistant
to support a diverse range of field and laboratory research activities in bioacoustics and sensory biology. This position will contribute to multidisciplinary research focused on understanding marine soundscapes, the effects of noise on marine life, and the sensory capabilities of marine organisms.

The successful candidate will work across multiple projects and research teams and should be comfortable operating in a dynamic environment that includes laboratory research, field operations, data analysis, and scientific outreach. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a broad portfolio of research involving marine bioacoustics, sensory biology, acoustic ecology, field science, data science, and emerging analytical technologies while working alongside interdisciplinary research teams at WHOI.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

Support acoustic studies investigating the effects of noise on marine life.
Assist with coral reef soundscape studies and related acoustic data analyses.
Support collection, organization, management, and quality control of research data.
Conduct acoustic analyses, including acoustic calibration and soundscape analysis.
Support machine learning analyses, particularly those involving acoustic and soundscape datasets.
Assist with field research activities, including SCUBA diving, small boat operations, equipment deployment, and other field logistics.
Support neurophysiological and electrophysiological experiments designed to measure the hearing abilities of marine fauna.
Assist with animal handling, husbandry, and zoological research activities as needed.
Contribute to the development, testing, and use of research tools and instrumentation.
Support data management and analysis involving large and complex datasets.
Assist with scientific outreach and related project activities.
Work collaboratively with multiple research teams while also independently managing assigned responsibilities.
Balance priorities and manage time effectively across several complementary projects.
Adapt to changing research needs, field conditions, and project priorities.

Required Education & Experience

Bachelor’s in Marine Science, Bioengineering, Biology, Engineering, or a related field.
Demonstrated interest in and ability to contribute to interdisciplinary research spanning marine biology, bioacoustics, engineering, and data science.
Ability and willingness to work in a variety of laboratory, field, and marine research environments, including conditions that may require flexibility in scheduling and work location.

Desired Experience

Master’s degree in Marine Science, Bioengineering, Biology, Engineering, or a related field.
Certified SCUBA diver with demonstrated diving proficiency and experience; AAUS certification is preferred.
MATLAB and related scientific programming or coding experience.
Acoustic analysis and bioacoustics experience.
Experience conducting acoustic calibrations.
Machine learning analysis, preferably involving acoustic or soundscape data.
Experience working with large datasets and scientific data management.
Small boat operation and related field research experience.
Marine biology experience combined with engineering, instrumentation, or research tool development.
Animal handling, husbandry, or zoological research experience.
Neurophysiology or electrophysiology experience.
Experience supporting field-based marine research.
Experience working in dynamic research environments and across multiple research teams.

jobs.title: Centaurs Research Assistant
jobs.description:
POSITION ANNOUNCEMENT

CENTAUR Research Assistant

Temporary Position

Lowell Observatory Research Assistants perform research in support of Lowell scientists. This position will be supervised by Dr. Nick Moskovitz who will ensure the Research Assistant makes adequate progress, but the ability to independently solve problems will be required.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The research assistant will work in collaboration with Dr. Moskovitz and other project team members on observational studies of Centaurs using new and archival astronomical data. Centaurs are a transient population of small bodies with orbits between that of Neptune and Jupiter. The motivation of this project is to better understand the processes at play effecting the surfaces of small solar system bodies as they evolve from the trans-Neptunian region towards the inner solar system. The project has two primary objectives:

1.      Performing telescopic observations to measure the optical colors of Centaurs that are similar in size to Jupiter Family Comets (<20 km) in order to investigate the relationship between size, color, and inferred surface properties. This aspect of the project includes opportunities to use the Large Monolithic Imager on the Lowell Discovery Telescope.
2.      Searching for cometary activity by stacking archival fits images of serendipitously observed Centaurs.

QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPECTATIONS

Regular meetings with project team members are expected, but in general the Assistant will be encouraged to work independently. They must be able to prioritize tasks, set schedules, troubleshoot problems, and complete complex tasks on time and within deadlines.
The Research Assistant must have experience in the use of computers for analysis of data. Familiarity with the Python programming language is strongly desired.
Applicants should describe in their cover letter relevant prior experience, reason for interest in this position, and how it may fit into their long-term career plans.
This is expected to be a 1-year, part time temporary position supported through an existing NASA grant, with possibility for extension up to 3 years based on performance and funding availability. The Assistant will work an average of 10 hours per week, but will have flexibility in deciding the specific scheduling of hours in any given week.
The Research Assistant is expected to reflect the professional and collegial environment the Observatory strives to maintain.

EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION

Minimum requirements for this position are to be working towards obtaining a bachelor’s degree in physics, astrophysics, astronomy, or related field.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Working in a laboratory environment, operating systems via computer interfaces as well as manual valves and switches, sometimes sitting for extended periods, working with computers for programming and data analysis tasks, and regularly meeting with team members via telecon and in person to report progress and discuss strategy. It will be necessary to move through the Flagstaff campus at 7,000’ elevation, sometimes on uneven terrain.

Job Summary

The Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences (CIRES) at the University of Colorado Boulder is seeking a Professional Research Assistant (Associate Scientist) to generate real-time ensemble cluster and sensitivity analysis tools from convection-allowing ensemble forecast datasets related to heavy precipitation, temperature, and other mesoscale variables of interest to the Weather Prediction Center (WPC) for use by operational forecasters within the National Weather Service (NWS). This position will also involve developing and disseminating training materials associated with probabilistic forecast tools, and assisting with ensemble post-processing workflows for applying new products in NOAA Testbed experiments. The Associate Scientist will interact with Federal WPC staff, NOAA scientists and forecasters, CIRES employees working at WPC, and external partners within the academic community and NOAA Labs such as Global Systems Laboratory (GSL) and Physical Systems Laboratory (PSL).

WPC is located in College Park, MD, within the NOAA Center for Weather and Climate Prediction (NCWCP). The NCWCP is a highly collaborative environment containing several NOAA organizations, including the Office of Modeling and Development (OMD), Ocean and Tsunami Center (OTC), and WPC’s Extended Prediction Division (EPD). This position performs novel research, transitions research projects to operations, serves as Principal Investigator (PI) or co-PI on funded projects, and collaborates with external partners.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

CIRES is an internationally recognized leader in innovative environmental science and research and is located at the University of Colorado Boulder. At CIRES, more than 900 environmental science professionals work to understand the dynamic Earth system, including people’s relationship with the planet. CIRES has partnered with NOAA since 1967, and our areas of expertise include weather and climate, changes at Earth’s poles, air quality and atmospheric chemistry, water resources, solid Earth sciences, and more. Our vision is to be instrumental in ensuring a sustainable future environment by advancing scientific and societal understanding of the Earth system.

The Weather Prediction Center (WPC) provides national weather situational awareness and precipitation expertise to enable readiness for hazardous weather events from seasons to minutes. WPC is the “Foundation of the Nation’s Weather Story,” providing National Decision Support products for Emergency Management, Aviation, Media, and the general public.

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

Identify and develop short-range ensemble-based tools that will assist in the preparation of forecasts. (30%)
Participate in the maintenance and enhancement of WPC's operational forecast tools. (20%)
Support a collaborative team to develop and fully transition to operations convection-allowing probabilistic forecast tools for short-range weather hazards. (20%)
Develop training materials to assist users in the transition of new tools and approaches into operations. (20%)
Collaborate on proposals, contribute through scientific publications, collaborate with colleagues, and attend various workshops and conferences. (10%)

What You Should Know

Applicants requiring visa sponsorship now or in the future will not be considered for this position.
Applicants must be currently authorized to legally work in the United States on a full-time basis.
The targeted start date is November 1, 2026.
Normal working hours will be observed except for occasional irregular hours during data collection or conferences/workshops conducted at remote sites.
The new hire will be employed by CIRES with technical oversight provided by WPC management. This role works independently and determines action to be taken in handling all but unusual situations. The incumbent is expected to serve as a leader of scientific or technical experiments, groups, or teams; therefore, strong teamwork and leadership skills are vital.
This role is based at the WPC in Riverdale Park, MD, but remote work within the United States will be considered.
Selected finalists will be required to pass a federal background check for site access.

What We Can Offer

CIRES can offer a generous compensation package.
The annual hiring salary range for this position is $60,000 - $97,000. Salary is commensurate with education and experience and determined based on our CIRES internal career track classification.
Some relocation funds are available to help offset expenses, following CIRES and the University of Colorado’s relocation processes and procedures.
CIRES and the University of Colorado Boulder offer a robust training curriculum, opportunities for professional development, and a Mentorship Program.
Boulder is a vibrant community with access to mountain parks, dog parks, miles of trails, rivers, lakes, cafes, restaurants, boutiques, theaters, museums, and sports venues.
As an employee at CU Boulder, you receive a pass allowing free access to the regional public transit system , which is an outstanding network of buses and light rail systems that provide service within Boulder and connect to Denver, the Denver airport, and surrounding communities.

Benefits

At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class outdoor recreation. Explore additional perks and programs through the CU Advantage program.

Be Statements

Be empowered. Be informed. Be Boulder.

What We Require

A bachelor's degree in meteorology, atmospheric science, or related field, with at least two years of directly relevant experience (or a master’s degree in meteorology, atmospheric science, or related field).
Experience working with, analyzing, and applying statistical methods to large meteorological datasets (e.g., GRIB, NetCDF).
Experience working in Linux and high-performance computing environments.

What You Will Need

Strong analytical and programming skills, including proficiency in Python and shell scripting.
Strong relationship-building and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage forecasters and incorporate their feedback into product development.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.
Demonstrated commitment to contributing to an inclusive and supportive work environment.

What We Would Like You To Have

Please note that while the position details both required skills and desired skills, applicants do not need to have all of the desired skills and experience to be considered for this position. If you meet the minimum qualifications, have passion for the work, along with experience in a related field, you are encouraged to apply. We provide on-the-job training for any additional skills or knowledge that become relevant to the position.

A master's degree or higher in Meteorology, Atmospheric Science, or a related field, with at least one year of relevant experience.
Experience applying statistical methods to extreme weather events.
Experience with ensemble prediction systems and their application to hazardous weather diagnosis and forecasting.
Experience with ensemble clustering and sensitivity analysis.
Demonstrated ability to develop, implement, and maintain real-time product workflows.
Experience preparing peer-reviewed manuscripts and competitive research proposals.
Willingness to contribute to web development.

Special Instructions

To Apply, Please Submit The Following Materials

Resume or CV;
Cover letter addressed to the Search Committee briefly describing your qualifications, professional goals, and specific interest in this position;
Although not needed at the time of application, please be ready to submit contact information for 5 professional references. All information is kept confidential and shared only with the members of the search committee.

If you are selected as the finalist, your degree will be verified by the CU Boulder Campus Human Resources department using an approved online vendor. If your degree was obtained outside of the United States, please submit a translated version as an optional attachment.

Please apply by September 4, 2026
for consideration.

Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For consideration, please apply through CU Boulder Jobs .

Job Description

Your Role

The Privacy Office is responsible for development, implementation, and oversight of Blue Shield’s Privacy Program. The Privacy Program ensures that Blue Shield and its affiliated covered entities, including Blue Shield of California Promise Health Plan, are in compliance with state and federal privacy laws and regulations, including the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act of 2009 (HITECH), and California’s Confidentiality of Medical Information Act (CMIA). The Privacy Program Specialist, Consultant reports to the Privacy Office Sr. Manager and plays an essential role in advancing and enforcing Blue Shield’s Privacy Program.

Responsibilities

Your Work

In this role, you will:

Be responsible for the oversight of Blue Shield's compliance with state and federal privacy laws, including the privacy component of HIPAA and HITECH
The majority of this role involves leading assigned privacy investigations, timely and accurately document case files, direct investigations into root cause analysis, address mitigation, and work with impacted business units to develop and complete corrective action for remediation and to minimize risk of recurrence
Consult with internal clients to review and provide privacy guidance about proposed projects and initiatives and serve as a privacy subject matter expert
Respond to privacy-related requests and inquiries
Develop and assist with the implementation of workforce privacy training programs, privacy policies, desk-level procedures, resource guides, job aids, and other educational tools
Act as a liaison with regulatory enforcement agencies to address technical assistance letters, investigation compliance reviews, audits, and other related reviews
Assist, evaluate, and determine appropriateness of ad hoc requests from internal clients to disclose protected health information (PHI) to third parties and/or to allow third parties access to, or use of, Blue Shield PHI
Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Your Knowledge and Experience

Required

Requires a bachelor’s degree or High School Diploma/GED and 4 years of additional relevant experience in lieu of a degree
Requires 7 years of prior relevant experience
Requires prior experience in healthcare privacy, cybersecurity incident management, investigative services, or another related field
Requires a solid understanding of state and federal privacy laws, including HIPAA/HITECH, CMIA, and privacy-related consumer protections laws, such as the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), as well as knowledge of Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) privacy requirements for Medi-Cal Managed Care Health Plans and Centers for Medicare or Medi-Cal and Medicaid (CMS) Medicare or Medi-Cal Managed Care Plans
Requires excellent organizational skills and strong independent judgment, problem-solving, critical and analytical thinking skills, including an exceptional “moral compass” and work ethic
Requires ability to work collaboratively in a team, perform duties with minimal supervision, multi-task, and to deliver a quality work product in a highly regulated, demanding, and constantly changing corporate environment
Requires proficiency in Microsoft Word, Access, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

Preferred

Possesses extensive experience in directly handling investigations
Privacy healthcare-related experience that includes a familiarity with Privacy Impact Assessments and Data Protection Impact Assessments; auditing and monitoring; investigating, managing, and reporting privacy incidents; health information management
CIPP/US Certification or HCCA CHPC Certification
Experience and knowledge of compliance or privacy incident management software

Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in-office time based on business need.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Product Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Hi, we're CompanyCam.

We're a simple-to-use photo documentation and productivity app for contractors of all commercial and home services industries. Packed with intuitive functionality, CompanyCam facilitates unparalleled communication and accountability across a contractor's entire business. We're committed to providing a consumer-grade, game-changing experience that helps our users build trust within their company and with their customers.

But don't let that corporate description fool you—the people behind our buttoned-up product are laid-back (but hardworking), genuine, and kickass, and you could be one of them!

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Data Analyst
to be a strategic partner to our product teams and make sure data sits at the core of how we make decisions. In this role, you'll lead data-driven initiatives, design scalable experimentation frameworks, and champion the Continuous Discovery Habits philosophy across Product, Engineering, and Design.

You'll hold teams accountable to product metrics, assumption testing, and experimentation best practices while mentoring other analysts and influencing roadmaps through clear, compelling storytelling with data. This role blends analytical depth, experimentation strategy, and cross-functional leadership in a fast-paced SaaS environment.

Location: This is a remote position. You must live and work permanently in the U.S. to be considered.

What You'll Do

Lead continuous discovery efforts by guiding PMs in defining and measuring success metrics, running assumption tests, and building iterative learning into how they work
Design robust experimentation frameworks, evaluate experiment results, and iterate on key hypotheses
Build scalable product analytics frameworks that standardize how teams make data-driven decisions
Enable self-service analytics by improving access to data through Metabase, Amplitude, and Secoda so teams can explore product insights independently
Mentor junior analysts on statistical methodology, experimentation best practices, and storytelling with data
Present insights and strategic recommendations to senior leadership regularly to influence product roadmaps
Champion best practices for both Product Managers and internal data teams around data-driven decision making, experimentation, data governance, and standardization
Leverage SQL, dbt, and Snowplow to transform, and analyze product data
Connect data insights to broader business strategy and communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders
Help foster a culture of experimentation, curiosity, and data-driven learning across Product and Engineering teams

The Impact You'll Have

At CompanyCam, your work makes a real impact.
Whether you're writing code, supporting customers, or designing experiences, your contributions directly shape the product we deliver and the people we serve. We're building something that helps real people solve real problems—and we believe that kind of work is best done by a team that reflects the world around us. I n this role, you'll drive impact by:

Raising the bar on how product teams define, measure, and act on success metrics
Making experimentation faster, more rigorous, and more trusted across the org
Influencing product roadmaps with insights that tie directly to business strategy
Scaling analytics practices so decision-making quality holds as we grow
Leveling up other analysts through mentorship and shared best practices

What You'll Bring

5+ years of experience in product analytics, data analytics, or a similar role
Strong proficiency in SQL, dbt, Snowplow, Amplitude, and Secoda (or equivalent tools)
Experience with A/B testing, hypothesis-driven research, and experiment design
Expertise in statistical modeling, causal inference, and data visualization
Experience designing and implementing analytics frameworks for scalable decision-making
Strong leadership skills with the ability to influence product teams and executives through insights and strategic recommendations
Proficiency in storytelling with data and translating insights into strategy
Prior experience in SaaS or fast-growing tech environments preferred
Comfortable working in a high-autonomy, high-accountability environment
Passion for fostering a culture of experimentation and data-driven learning
A continuous growth-mindset, with a focus on learning, embracing challenges, and continuously improving.
A knack for creativity and innovation, bringing fresh ideas to the table and solving complex problems.

Benefits & Compensation

This is a salaried position at CompanyCam. Our starting salary range is $130,000-$140,000
per year and is based on experience. We also offer meaningful equity and other benefits.

CompanyCam is an equal-opportunity employer committed to respect, inclusion, and growth. We work hard, take responsibility, and support each other. Great ideas come from all backgrounds, and we carefully consider every applicant without regard to personal characteristics or traits. Even if your work experience doesn't align perfectly, we encourage you to apply. What really matters to us is your potential, your passion, and your commitment to learning, innovation, and contributing meaningfully to our team.

For any accommodations or technical issues related to the online application or interview process, please email jobs@companycam.com and we'll respond promptly. Please do not include any medical or health information in your message.

. To be considered for a position, you must apply directly through our careers page.

Position Summary:

The Quality Management Data Analyst III is a senior-level analytics role responsible for leading complex data analysis, Power BI report development, data validation, and quality reporting initiatives that support hospital operations, regulatory readiness, patient safety, performance improvement, and strategic decision-making. This position partners with Quality, clinical, operational, infection prevention, regulatory, and leadership stakeholders to translate business and clinical questions into reliable data products, clear insights, and governed, sustainable reporting solutions that are maintained throughout their life cycle. The Quality Management Data Analyst III serves as a subject-matter-expert for Microsoft Power BI, SQL-based analysis, data definitions, report modernization, and quality analytics standards, while helping build internal analytics capacity.

Position Requirements:

Licensure/Certification/Registrations: Microsoft Power BI and/or Microsoft Fabric Data Engineer certification preferred.
Education: Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in analytics, data science, information systems, healthcare administration, business, public health, clinical discipline, or related field required.
Experience: Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in data analysis, business intelligence, reporting, or healthcare analytics required. Experience supporting quality, regulatory, patient safety, performance improvement, or hospital operations strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience using SQL to query, validate, reconcile, and assess data integrity across multiple databases required. Advanced experience designing and maintaining Microsoft Power BI reports, dashboards, semantic models, DAX measures, and Power Query transformations required. Experience publishing, troubleshooting, and optimizing governed Power BI reporting solutions required. Experience with dimensional modeling, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Purview, Epic, FHIR, data governance, or healthcare data warehouse environments preferred.
Skills & Abilities: Advanced analytical, technical, communication, and project management skills. Ability to independently lead complex analytics projects from requirements gathering through design, validation, deployment, adoption, and ongoing maintenance. Strong understanding of data quality, metric definitions, regulatory reporting, confidentiality, HIPAA-sensitive data handling, and stakeholder communication. Ability to explain complex technical concepts to clinical, operational, and executive audiences. Ability to manage competing priorities, mentor others, facilitate consensus around data definitions, and maintain a high degree of accuracy, dependability, and attention to detail. Proactively identify reporting gaps and efficiently move projects from intake through adoption with limited direction.

Essential Functions:

Enterprise Analytics and Reporting

Lead the design, development, validation, implementation, and ongoing optimization of enterprise reporting and analytics solutions that support clinical, operational, administrative, financial, regulatory, foundation, and strategic business functions.
Translate complex organizational questions into analytical frameworks, metrics, dashboards, data models, and actionable recommendations that support data-informed decisions at the department, committee, and executive levels.
Independently evaluate and scope analytics requests and recommend priorities in collaboration with leadership and stakeholders, considering organizational value and strategic alignment, regulatory urgency, data readiness, technical feasibility, resource requirements, and long-term supportability.
Use SQL, Power Query, DAX, and related tools to extract, transform, join, reconcile, and validate data from hospital systems, data warehouse environments, foundation or business systems, and other approved data sources.
Develop reporting solutions that balance accuracy, usability, sustainability, performance, confidentiality, and the needs of both technical and non-technical audiences.

Power BI and Microsoft Fabric Leadership

Serve as the hospital's subject-matter-expert for Microsoft Power BI and reporting, including semantic model design, DAX development, data visualization standards, report governance, workspace organization, and report life cycle management.
Support organization-wide implementation, adoption, and effective use of Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric by helping define reporting standards, development practices, access expectations, documentation requirements, and sustainable support models.
Collaborate with data owners and operational stakeholders to align reporting solutions with Microsoft Fabric architecture, approved data sources, data security expectations, and enterprise analytics priorities.
Establish, document, and follow appropriate development, testing, user acceptance, deployment, change-control, and retirement practices for assigned reporting assets, consistent with organizational standards.
Review and improve report logic, semantic models, data refresh processes, measure definitions, dashboard usability, and performance to strengthen trust and consistency in organizational reporting.
Monitor the reliability of assigned production reporting solutions, investigate failures or material discrepancies, communicate impacts to affected stakeholders, and coordinate timely correction and validation.
Evaluate reporting needs and recommend whether solutions should be addressed through enterprise dashboards, departmental Power BI reports, governed semantic models, manual analysis, or other approved reporting approaches.

Data Governance, Data Quality, and Standards

Actively participate in data governance activities, including metric standardization, business glossary development, data cataloging, reporting inventory maintenance, data lineage documentation, stewardship discussions, and validation of approved data definitions.
Establish and maintain clear metric definitions, business rules, calculation logic, source system notes, data lineage, validation evidence, and report documentation to support consistent interpretation across departments and reporting domains.
Identify data discrepancies, investigate root causes, communicate limitations, recommend corrections or process improvements, and verify that changes are implemented appropriately.
Promote responsible data use by applying organizational policies, HIPAA requirements, foundation data stewardship expectations, confidentiality standards, approved access controls, and role-based reporting requirements throughout the analytics life cycle.
Facilitate consensus among stakeholders when definitions, data sources, business rules, or reporting expectations differ across departments.

Training, Consultation, and Data Literacy

Develop and maintain training materials, quick reference guides, report documentation, office hours, and user support resources that improve Power BI adoption, reporting literacy, and consistent interpretation of dashboards across the hospital.
Design and deliver education sessions, demonstrations, and consultative support for leaders, clinicians, administrative teams, foundation staff, analysts, fellows, interns, and departmental report developers.
Coach colleagues on dashboard navigation, appropriate use of measures, interpretation of trends and variation, limitations of available data, and responsible use of self-service reporting tools.
Mentor analysts and project contributors on report development practices, data validation methods, documentation expectations, visualization design, and analytics problem-solving.
Serve as a consultative partner for departments seeking to modernize reports, clarify metrics, improve reporting workflows, or increase local data literacy.

Strategic Partnership and Organizational Support

Partner with executive, clinical, operational, administrative, and foundation leaders to identify strategic reporting opportunities and translate organizational priorities into reliable analytics solutions.
Support multidisciplinary committees, project teams, regulatory readiness efforts, operational improvement initiatives, foundation reporting priorities, and enterprise analytics projects through timely and actionable analysis.
Evaluate report adoption, usability, stakeholder understanding, and ongoing business value, and use feedback to improve reporting products, training, and support approaches.
Provide clear written and verbal explanations of findings, assumptions, limitations, risks, and recommendations to audiences with varying levels of technical expertise.
Maintain current knowledge of healthcare analytics, business intelligence, Microsoft Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, data governance, federal and state requirements, accreditation standards, and emerging reporting practices relevant to the organization.
